# Page: Overview

# Overview

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

</details>



Foldseek is a high-performance tool designed for fast and sensitive comparisons of large protein structure sets. It enables rapid searching and clustering of protein structures with performance up to 20,000 times faster than traditional structural aligners while maintaining comparable sensitivity [README.md:2-7](). Foldseek supports monomer and multimer searches, runs on CPU, and leverages GPU acceleration for enhanced speed [README.md:3]().

Sources: [README.md:2-11](), [src/foldseek.cpp:5-9]()

## What is Foldseek?

Foldseek is specialized software for structural bioinformatics that allows users to:

- **Search**: Compare protein structures against massive databases such as AlphaFoldDB or the Protein Data Bank (PDB), quickly retrieving structural homologs [README.md:66-67]().
- **Cluster**: Group similar protein structures into clusters to reduce redundancy and analyze structural diversity at large scale [README.md:42-47]().
- **Multimer Support**: Perform complex alignments and scoring on multi-chain protein complexes (multimers), enabling analysis beyond monomers [README.md:51-58]().
- **Sequence-to-Structure Search**: Efficiently predict 3Di structural sequences from raw amino acid sequences using an integrated protein language model, enabling ultra-fast and sensitive structure searches without available 3D coordinates [README.md:3](), [src/foldseek.cpp:15-21]().

Sources: [README.md:2-11](), [src/foldseek.cpp:5-21]()

## System Architecture

Foldseek's architecture is modular and command-driven, extending the MMseqs2 framework to handle large structural databases, parameter management, and parallel execution efficiently. Commands are registered and dispatched dynamically, supported by a shared parameter singleton (`LocalParameters`) [src/foldseek.cpp:15-22]().

### Code-to-System Mapping

This diagram maps core system concepts to corresponding key source files and components in the codebase:

```mermaid
flowchart TD

    end

    end

    ClusterSH --> ClusterCPP

```

Sources: [src/foldseek.cpp:15-22](), [data/structdatabases.sh:1-30]()

## Command System Overview

Foldseek organizes functionality into a layered command hierarchy to balance usability and advanced control. It offers simplified `easy-*` workflows, core structural analysis commands, database management tools, multimer analysis utilities, and format converters [src/foldseek.cpp:15-22]().

"Easy" commands wrap complex pipelines into a single user-facing interface for convenience, while core commands provide granular control and extension points [src/foldseek.cpp:15-22]().

For installation details and initial setup guidance, see [Installation and Getting Started](#1.1). For an explanation of command organization and workflows, see [Command Structure](#1.2). For common usage examples and command patterns, see [Basic Usage Examples](#1.3).

Sources: [src/foldseek.cpp:15-22](), [README.md:59-60]()

## Database System

Foldseek stores structural data in a custom multi-file database format combining amino acid sequences, 3Di structural descriptors, and Cα coordinates for spatial context [README.md:94-100]().

The database is constructed via database creation modules, converting PDB, mmCIF, tar archives, or TSV lists into indexed Foldseek structure databases with efficient coordinate compression and feature encoding [data/structdatabases.sh:89-178](), [README.md:94-100]().

### Data Flow Diagram for Database Creation and Usage

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input_Formats"
        PDB["\".pdb / .cif files\""]
        FASTA["\".fasta files\""]
    end

    subgraph "Pipeline"
        Enc["\"3Di Encoder\""]
        Comp["\"Coordinate Compression\""]
    end

    subgraph "Database_Files"
        AA["\"_seq (Amino Acid sequences)\""]
        SS["\"_ss (3Di sequences)\""]
        CA["\"_ca (Ca coordinates)\""]
        HDR["\"_h (Headers / metadata)\""]
    end

    PDB --> createdb
    FASTA --> createdb
    createdb --> Enc --> Comp --> AA & SS & CA & HDR
```

Foldseek provides automated download scripts (`structdatabases.sh`) with a selection of pre-built public structural databases available for download, such as AlphaFoldDB variants, PDB, CATH50, and others [data/structdatabases.sh:89-178]().

Sources: [data/structdatabases.sh:89-178](), [README.md:38-41, 94-100]()

## Performance Features and Hardware Support

- **GPU Acceleration:** Foldseek supports Nvidia GPU acceleration (Ampere generation or newer recommended) for faster search computations, with fallback to CPU-only mode [README.md:13, 91-93]().
- **Memory Management Options:** Users can configure different memory modes, such as disabling Cα coordinate details to save RAM at some cost to hit ranking precision, or fully exhaustive single-query modes using prefilter adjustments [README.md:95-104]().
- **High Parallelism:** Designed to scale to large protein structure datasets with multithreading and optimized SIMD support [README.md:3]().

Sources: [README.md:3, 13, 91-104]()

This page provides comprehensive technical instructions for installing Foldseek on multiple platforms, outlines system requirements, explains the internal build and runtime architecture, and guides initial setup including database preparation and running example searches.

Foldseek is built on top of the MMseqs2 framework and offers fast, sensitive protein structure searching, clustering, and supports GPU acceleration and sequence input via protein language models.

---

## System Requirements

### Hardware Requirements

| Component | Details |
|-----------|---------|
| **CPU** | x86_64 with at least SSE4.1 support; AVX2 highly recommended for optimal performance in 3Di encoding and alignment. ARM64 (AArch64) supported on Linux and Apple Silicon. |
| **GPU** | Optional NVIDIA GPU: Ampere generation or newer for full GPU acceleration; Turing generation supported at reduced speed. Requires `glibc >= 2.17` and NVIDIA driver `>= 525.60.13`. Not all binaries support older GPUs. |
| **RAM** | Memory needs depend on the database size and search mode. Refer to the modes below. |

### Memory Modes and Formulas

| Mode | Description | RAM Formula | RAM Example (54M AFDB50) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Default | With Cα coordinate info (default) | `(6 bytes Cα + 1 byte 3Di + 1 byte AA) * database residues` | ~151 GB |
| Light | Without Cα coordinate info, disables `--sort-by-structure-bits 0` | `(1 byte 3Di + 1 byte AA) * database residues` | ~35 GB |
| Single Query Prefilter | Uses `--prefilter-mode 1`, not memory-limited and multithreaded | N/A (depends on query) | Variable |

> The default mode retains structural coordinate information and is recommended for best hit ranking quality.

Sources: [README.md:71-102]()

---

## Installation Methods

### 1. Pre-built Binaries (Recommended for Most Users)

Foldseek offers statically linked, platform-specific binaries for quick installation without compilation.

```bash
# Linux AVX2 (x86_64)
wget https://mmseqs.com/foldseek/foldseek-linux-avx2.tar.gz
tar xvzf foldseek-linux-avx2.tar.gz
export PATH=$(pwd)/foldseek/bin/:$PATH

# Linux ARM64
wget https://mmseqs.com/foldseek/foldseek-linux-arm64.tar.gz
tar xvzf foldseek-linux-arm64.tar.gz
export PATH=$(pwd)/foldseek/bin/:$PATH

# Linux AVX2 + GPU build (glibc >= 2.17, Nvidia driver >= 525.60.13)
wget https://mmseqs.com/foldseek/foldseek-linux-gpu.tar.gz
tar xvfz foldseek-linux-gpu.tar.gz
export PATH=$(pwd)/foldseek/bin/:$PATH

# MacOS Universal (Intel + Apple Silicon)
wget https://mmseqs.com/foldseek/foldseek-osx-universal.tar.gz
tar xvzf foldseek-osx-universal.tar.gz
export PATH=$(pwd)/foldseek/bin/:$PATH
```

More binaries are available at [https://mmseqs.com/foldseek](https://mmseqs.com/foldseek).

#### Notes:
* Static linking minimizes dependency issues.
* GPU binaries require compatible hardware and software stack.

Sources: [README.md:74-88](), [Dockerfile:1-83]()

---

### 2. Conda Package Manager

Foldseek is available on Bioconda channel for Linux and macOS.

```bash
conda install -c conda-forge -c bioconda foldseek
```

Sources: [README.md:86-88]()

---

### 3. Docker

Pre-built multi-architecture Docker images simplify environment setup, including GPU-enabled variants.

- Standard Foldseek: `ghcr.io/steineggerlab/foldseek:latest`
- GPU-enabled Foldseek (CUDA 12): `ghcr.io/steineggerlab/foldseek:latest-cuda12`

The Dockerfile uses a multi-stage build that compiles SSE4.1 and AVX2 optimized binaries separately, then selects the appropriate one at runtime via the `entrypoint` wrapper script (`util/foldseek_wrapper.sh`), detecting CPU capabilities by inspecting `/proc/cpuinfo`.

This ensures performance tuning for diverse hardware automatically.

Title: "Docker Build and Runtime Flow"
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Build Stage ["Build Stage (Dockerfile:2-64)"]
        D["Debian Bookworm-Slim Base"] --> R["Rust Toolchain Setup"]
        R --> C["Compile for ARM64 and x86_64 via cmake"]
    end

    subgraph Final Image ["Final Image Execution"]
        Binaries["/usr/local/bin/foldseek_avx2, /usr/local/bin/foldseek_sse41, /usr/local/bin/foldseek_arch"]
        Wrapper["util/foldseek_wrapper.sh (entrypoint)"]
    end

    C --> Binaries
    Binaries --> Wrapper
    Wrapper -->|"grep flags /proc/cpuinfo"| Exec["Executes optimal binary"]
```

Sources: [Dockerfile:1-83](), [.github/workflows/docker.yml:1-141](), [util/foldseek_wrapper.sh:1-10]()

---

### 4. Building From Source

For developers or advanced users needing customization.

#### Prerequisites

- C++ compiler with C++11 support
- Rust toolchain (required for `block-aligner`)
- CMake (>=3.15)
- Optional: CUDA toolkit for GPU support

#### Build System Overview

Foldseek uses CMake to integrate multiple submodules and libraries:

- Core MMseqs2 framework (`lib/mmseqs`)
- 3Di structural encoding (`lib/3di`)
- Structural tools (`lib/pulchra`, `lib/tmalign`)
- Neural network inference (`lib/kerasify`)
- ProstT5 protein language model (`lib/prostt5`)
- Database compression support (`lib/foldcomp`)
- Optional: StructTTY viewer (`lib/structty`)

Title: "Foldseek Component and Library Dependencies"
```mermaid
graph TD
    FS_EXE["foldseek (foldseek.cpp)"]
    BASE["FoldseekBase.cpp"]
    LC["LocalCommandDeclarations.h"]
    WF["Workflow Controllers (src/workflow)"]

    MM["lib/mmseqs (MMseqs2 Core)"]
    DI["lib/3di (3Di encoder)"]
    PUL["lib/pulchra (Atom Reconstruction)"]
    KER["lib/kerasify (NN Inference)"]
    TM["lib/tmalign (TM-score alignment)"]
    PT5["lib/prostt5 (Protein LM integration)"]
    FC["lib/foldcomp (DB compression)"]
    ST["lib/structty (Optional viewer)"]

    FS_EXE --> BASE
    BASE --> LC
    BASE --> WF
    BASE --> MM
    BASE --> DI
    BASE --> PUL
    BASE --> KER
    BASE --> TM
    BASE --> FC
    WF --> PT5
    BASE --> ST
```

Sources: [src/CMakeLists.txt:3-25](), [CMakeLists.txt:31-118]()

#### Build Instructions

1. Clone repository with submodules:

```bash
git clone --recursive https://github.com/steineggerlab/foldseek.git
cd foldseek
```

2. Configure build with CMake:

- CPU-only build (default):

```bash
cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release .
```

- Enable GPU support (if CUDA toolkit installed):

```bash
cmake -DENABLE_CUDA=1 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release .
```

- Static linking of dependencies:

```bash
cmake -DFORCE_STATIC_DEPS=1 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release .
```

3. Build executable(s):

```bash
make -j$(nproc)
```

4. The executable `foldseek` will be in `src/`.

**Build Verification**

Run regression tests:

```bash
./regression/run_regression.sh ./src/foldseek examples
```

Sources: [azure-pipelines.yml:45-69](), [util/build_osx.sh:1-120](), [CMakeLists.txt:10-25]()

---

## Getting Started

### Database Preparation

Foldseek requires input structure databases in its own format, encoding structures to 3Di and sequence representations.

The `databases` command manages downloading and formatting of popular structural databases like PDB or AlphaFoldDB.

Example: Download and prepare PDB database

```bash
foldseek databases PDB pdb_dir tmp_dir
```

- `pdb_dir`: destination directory for database files
- `tmp_dir`: temporary working directory for intermediate files

This step encodes the structures into fast searchable formats for Foldseek.

Sources: [README.md:41-44]()

---

### Running a Simple Search

Convenience commands like `easy-search` automate the full pipeline of encoding, prefiltering, alignment, and output formatting.

Example command:

```bash
foldseek easy-search query.pdb target_db output.m8 tmp_dir
```

- `query.pdb`: input query structure(s)
- `target_db`: target Foldseek database directory
- `output.m8`: tab-separated result output
- `tmp_dir`: temporary directory for intermediate files

Title: "Easy-Search Workflow Data Flow"
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as User
    participant ES as easy-search (StructureSearch.cpp)
    participant DBencode as structcreatedb Module
    participant Prefilter as prefilter Module
    participant Align as align Module

    User->>ES: Run easy-search with inputs
    ES->>DBencode: Encode structures to 3Di + AA sequences
    DBencode-->>ES: Produce Foldseek format database
    ES->>Prefilter: Fast k-mer based 3Di prefiltering
    Prefilter-->>ES: Candidate alignments
    ES->>Align: 3Di+AA Smith-Waterman or TM-align rescoring
    Align-->>User: Tabulated search results (output.m8)
```

This process efficiently finds structural homologs with high sensitivity.

Sources: [README.md:31-38](), [src/workflow/StructureSearch.cpp:1-50]()

---

### Verification and Version Check

Verify correct installation and hardware support by querying the Foldseek version and enabled CPU features:

```bash
foldseek version
```

This outputs build information including CPU SIMD flags (SSE4.1, AVX2) and CUDA support.

Sources: [src/CMakeLists.txt:40-45]()

---

## Summary Table for Installation Options

| Installation Method | Command / Notes | Benefits | Notes |
|---------------------|-----------------|----------|-------|
| Pre-built binaries | Download and extract tarballs from mmseqs.com/foldseek | Fast setup, no build required | Use correct architecture binary |
| Conda | `conda install -c conda-forge -c bioconda foldseek` | Easy dependency management | Suitable for Linux/macOS |
| Docker (standard) | `docker pull ghcr.io/steineggerlab/foldseek:latest` | Containerized environment | Multi-arch support |
| Docker (GPU) | `docker pull ghcr.io/steineggerlab/foldseek:latest-cuda12` | GPU-accelerated searches | Requires NVIDIA GPU and drivers |
| Build from source | `cmake` + `make` in foldseek repo | Custom builds, development | Requires build tools and dependencies |

---

By following these detailed instructions, users can install Foldseek on a variety of platforms, prepare structure databases, and run efficient structure searches with high sensitivity leveraging CPU and GPU resources as available.

# Command Structure

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

## Purpose and Scope
This page details the organization of commands, workflows, and execution pathways in FoldSeek. FoldSeek employs a modular, command-driven architecture that bridges the MMseqs2 core framework with structure-specific bioinformatics routines. The system classifies operations into user-facing easy commands (`COMMAND_EASY`), core modular blocks (`COMMAND_MAIN`, `COMMAND_SET`), and hidden or utility sub-commands (`COMMAND_HIDDEN`), governed by a centralized parameter singleton and dispatched via unified registration vectors.

Sources: [src/foldseek.cpp:1-22](), [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:1-21](), [src/LocalParameters.h:18-26]()

---

## Overview of Command Organization & Registry

FoldSeek utilizes a layered command registry. The main entry point in `src/foldseek.cpp` initializes command handling by registering two command vectors: `baseCommands` (inherited from MMseqs2) and `foldseekCommands` (FoldSeek-specific).

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class FoldSeekMain {
        +init()
        +registerCommands(vector~Command~*)
    }
    class CommandRegistry {
        +std::vector~Command~ baseCommands
        +std::vector~Command~ foldseekCommands
    }
    class LocalParameters {
        +getLocalInstance()
        +initParameterSingleton()
    }
    FoldSeekMain --> LocalParameters : "calls initParameterSingleton"
    FoldSeekMain --> CommandRegistry : "registers foldseekCommands"
```

Title: Command Registration Architecture
Sources: [src/foldseek.cpp:15-22](), [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:17-21]()

---

## Command Categories and Mappings

FoldSeek commands are categorized by flags in the `Command` struct that govern their visibility, grouping, and execution behavior. These are declared in `src/FoldseekBase.cpp` and mapped to implementations listed in `src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h`.

| Category Flag    | Description                                      | Example Commands               |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| `COMMAND_EASY`   | High-level workflow wrappers for routine tasks   | `easy-search`, `easy-cluster`  |
| `COMMAND_MAIN`   | Primary core building blocks                     | `createdb`, `structuresearch`  |
| `COMMAND_SET`    | Set and index manipulation operations            | `createsubdb`, `createinterfacedb` |
| `COMMAND_HIDDEN` | Internal or specialized utility operations       | `structureto3didescriptor`, `filterdimerdb` |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    executable["foldseek executable"] --> dispatcher["Dispatcher src/foldseek.cpp"]
    dispatcher --> easy["COMMAND_EASY src/FoldseekBase.cpp"]
    dispatcher --> main["COMMAND_MAIN src/FoldseekBase.cpp"]
    dispatcher --> set["COMMAND_SET src/FoldseekBase.cpp"]
    dispatcher --> hidden["COMMAND_HIDDEN src/FoldseekBase.cpp"]

    easy --> easySearch["easystructuresearch src/workflow/EasyStructureSearch.cpp"]
    main --> structCreateDb["structcreatedb src/FoldseekBase.cpp"]
    set --> createInterfaceDb["createinterfacedb src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp"]
    hidden --> filterDimerDb["filterdimerdb src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h"]
```

Title: Command Dispatch and Code Mapping
Sources: [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:17-96](), [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h:6-44]()

---

## Easy-* Commands: Simplified Workflows

FoldSeek's `easy-*` commands (`COMMAND_EASY`) wrap multi-step pipelines into single user-facing commands. They automatically handle database conversion, searching, prefiltering, alignment, and formatting.

### Data Flow within `easy-search`
The `easy-search` interface invokes `easystructuresearch`, which orchestrates structure database creation (`structcreatedb`), structure searching (`structuresearch`), and alignment conversion (`structureconvertalis`).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    input["Input PDB/mmCIF Files"] --> createDb["structcreatedb src/FoldseekBase.cpp"]
    createDb --> search["structuresearch src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h"]
    search --> convert["structureconvertalis src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h"]
    convert --> output["Output Alignment .m8/.tsv"]
```

Title: easy-search Execution Pipeline
Sources: [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:92-95](), [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h:6-20]()

---

## Core Commands and Utility Sub-commands

Core commands (`COMMAND_MAIN`, `COMMAND_SET`) expose modular building blocks for advanced workflow construction:
- **`createdb` (`structcreatedb`)**: Converts raw structure inputs (PDB, mmCIF, tar archives, TSV lists) into binary FoldSeek databases containing sequence (`_ss`), coordinate (`_ca`), and header (`_h`) files [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:18-41]().
- **`createsubdb` (`createstructsubdb`)**: Extracts subsets of databases using ID lists [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:49-60]().
- **`createinterfacedb` (`createinterfacedb`)**: Orchestrates complex dimer interface database construction by executing embedded shell scripts (`createinterfacedb.sh`) alongside `createstructinterfacedb` [src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp:9-25](), [src/strucclustutils/createstructinterfacedb.cpp:35-42]().

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    cmdCall["createinterfacedb src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp"] --> parse["LocalParameters::parseParameters"]
    parse --> writeScript["FileUtil::writeFile createinterfacedb.sh"]
    writeScript --> exec["CommandCaller::execProgram createinterfacedb.sh"]
    exec --> subCmd["createstructinterfacedb src/strucclustutils/createstructinterfacedb.cpp"]
```

Title: Interface Database Creation Control Flow
Sources: [src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp:9-25](), [src/strucclustutils/createstructinterfacedb.cpp:35-45]()

---

## Parameter System Integration

All commands share a global configuration state managed through the singleton `LocalParameters` class, initialized at startup by `initParameterSingleton()` [src/foldseek.cpp:22](). Commands retrieve parameter definitions and option values via `LocalParameters::getLocalInstance()` [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:21-26]().

- Parameter definitions cover alignment types (`alignmentType`), TM-score thresholds (`tmScoreThr`), and coordinate storage modes (`coordStoreMode`) [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:11-26]().
- Database validators (`DbValidator`) ensure valid type matching across extended database flags such as `DBTYPE_CA_ALPHA` and `DBTYPE_TMSCORE` [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:10-16](), [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:9-14]().

Sources: [src/foldseek.cpp:22](), [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:18-35](), [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:6-26](), [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:8-15]()

---

# Basic Usage Examples

<details>

</details>



This page provides practical usage examples of commonly employed Foldseek commands to search, cluster, and handle protein structure data. It illustrates typical patterns using easy commands (`easy-search`, `easy-cluster`, `easy-multimersearch`), database download utilities, and example input files in the `example/` directory.

---

## Command Workflow Structure

Foldseek offers two main categories of commands:

- **Easy commands:** High-level wrappers (`easy-search`, `easy-cluster`, `easy-multimersearch`) that bundle multiple steps into single user-facing commands.
- **Core commands:** Modular building blocks (`createdb`, `search`, `cluster`), allowing customizable and flexible workflows.

The natural language CLI commands map directly to workflow controller classes, which further invoke shell-script pipelines to implement the workflows.

### Diagram: CLI Commands to Workflow Controllers to Shell Pipelines

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "NaturalLanguage/CLISpace"
        CLI_easys["foldseek easy-search / easy-cluster / easy-multimersearch"]
    end

    subgraph "CodeEntitySpace"
        EasyStructureSearch["Class: EasyStructureSearch"]
        StructureCluster["Class: StructureCluster"]
        MultimerSearch["Class: MultimerSearch"]
    end

    subgraph "Workflow Implementation"
        easystructsearch_sh["easystructuresearch.sh"]
        structurecluster_sh["structurecluster.sh"]
        multimersearch_sh["multimersearch.sh"]
    end

    CLI_easys -->|dispatch| EasyStructureSearch
    CLI_easys -->|dispatch| StructureCluster
    CLI_easys -->|dispatch| MultimerSearch

    EasyStructureSearch -.->|executes| easystructsearch_sh
    StructureCluster -.->|executes| structurecluster_sh
    MultimerSearch -.->|executes| multimersearch_sh
```

Sources: [README.md:59-64](), [src/workflow/EasyStructureSearch.cpp:28-30](), [src/workflow/StructureCluster.cpp:28-30](), [src/workflow/MultimerSearch.cpp:28-30]()

---

## Structure Search Examples

### Basic Structure Search Using easy-search

This example performs a structural comparison of a query against a database directory of structures, using files in the `example/` directory:

```bash
foldseek easy-search example/d1asha_ example/ aln tmpFolder
```

- `example/d1asha_`: query structure(s)
- `example/`: target structure database directory
- `aln`: output basename prefix
- `tmpFolder`: temporary directory for intermediate files

### Data Flow in easy-search

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    PDB["Input PDB Files ('example/d1asha_')"]
    DB["createdb: Build structure DB"]
    PRE["prefilter: Find candidate matches"]
    ALN["structurealign: Refined alignment (3Di + AA)"]
    OUT["Output: alignment result files (tabular, HTML, etc.)"]

    PDB --> DB
    DB --> PRE
    PRE --> ALN
    ALN --> OUT
```

Sources: [README.md:30-40](), [src/foldseek.cpp:1-22]()

### GPU Acceleration for Faster Searches

Foldseek supports GPU acceleration (NVIDIA Ampere or newer) for large-scale or faster queries:

```bash
foldseek easy-search example/d1asha_ example/ aln tmp --gpu 1 --prefilter-mode 1
```

Note the use of `--gpu 1` to enable GPU search, and `--prefilter-mode 1` for ungapped alignment prefiltering optimized for single queries.

> **Important:** For GPU-accelerated search, the structural database needs to be padded appropriately for best performance (see database commands below).

Sources: [README.md:64-68](), [README.md:91-93]()

### Output Format Modes

Foldseek supports different output formats controlled by the `--format-mode` option:

| Format Mode | Description                      | Example Command                                 |
|:------------|:--------------------------------|:------------------------------------------------|
| 0 (default) | Tab-separated alignment results | `foldseek easy-search … aln.m8 tmp`             |
| 3           | Interactive HTML report           | `foldseek easy-search … result.html tmp --format-mode 3` |
| 5           | Superpositioned Cα PDB files     | `foldseek easy-search … result_dir tmp --format-mode 5` |

Sources: [README.md:34-40]()

---

## Structure Clustering Examples

### Basic Clustering Using easy-cluster

Cluster all protein structures within a directory based on similarity with a selected coverage threshold:

```bash
foldseek easy-cluster example/ res tmp -c 0.9
```

- `example/`: input directory containing structure files to cluster
- `res`: output prefix for cluster results
- `tmp`: temporary folder
- `-c 0.9`: clustering coverage threshold (90% coverage required)

### Clustering Pipeline Components

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    KM["kmermatcher: fast candidate selection"]
    RES["structurerescorediagonal: 3Di rescoring"]
    CLU["clust: greedy clustering"]

    KM --> RES
    RES --> CLU
```

Sources: [README.md:45-50](), [src/workflow/StructureCluster.cpp:1-50]()

### Clustering Output Files

- `res_clu.tsv`: Cluster assignments listing cluster representative and member sequences.
- `res_repseq.fasta`: Fasta file containing representative sequences of detected clusters.
- `res_allseq.fasta`: Fasta of all cluster members grouped by cluster.

Sources: [README.md:46-50]()

---

## Multimer Processing Examples

Foldseek supports alignment and clustering of protein complexes (multimers) with the multimer search and cluster commands.

### Multimer Search Using easy-multimersearch

Search a multimeric complex against another complex or database:

```bash
foldseek easy-multimersearch example/1tim.pdb.gz example/8tim.pdb.gz result tmp
```

- `example/1tim.pdb.gz`: query complex structure file
- `example/8tim.pdb.gz`: target complex or database file
- `result`: output basename prefix
- `tmp`: temporary working directory

### Multimer Search Workflow

The multimer pipeline splits complexes into chains, conducts chain-vs-chain comparisons, and computes complex TM-scores by optimal chain mapping.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Split["Split complexes into chains"]
    Search["Chain-to-chain structure search"]
    ScoreMultimer["scoremultimer: chain mapping & TM-score calculation"]
    ComplexTM["Complex TM-score output"]

    Split --> Search
    Search --> ScoreMultimer
    ScoreMultimer --> ComplexTM
```

Sources: [README.md:51-56](), [README.md:11-12]()

---

## Database Download and Preparation

Foldseek provides a builtin command to download and prepare commonly used standard structural databases such as PDB, AlphaFoldDB, and CATH.

### Downloading e.g. PDB or AlphaFoldDB

```bash
foldseek databases PDB pdb tmp
foldseek databases Alphafold/Proteome afdb tmp
```

- `PDB`, `Alphafold/Proteome`: predefined selection keys for datasets
- `pdb`, `afdb`: output destination directory prefix
- `tmp`: temporary folder for downloads and extraction

This script internally downloads tarballs, extracts structure databases, and prepares them for Foldseek use.

Sources: [data/structdatabases.sh:81-179]()

### Creating Your Own Database from Local Files

Convert a directory of structure files into a Foldseek database:

```bash
foldseek createdb example/ myTargetDB
foldseek createindex myTargetDB tmp
```

- `createdb` processes input structure files into indexed database format.
- `createindex` creates necessary auxiliary indexing files for quick searching.

Sources: [README.md:42-44]()

### Using ProstT5 for FASTA to 3Di Conversion

Foldseek can convert protein sequences (FASTA) directly to 3Di structural descriptors using ProstT5 language model integration:

```bash
foldseek createdb input.fasta myDB --prostt5-model path/to/weights --gpu 1
```

This bypasses the need for experimentally or computationally determined structures to perform structure-like searches.

Sources: [README.md:3-3], [data/structdatabases.sh:171-178]()

---

## Example Files in `example/`

The `example/` directory contains sample PDB files (`example/1tim.pdb.gz`, `example/8tim.pdb.gz`) and pre-indexed example databases (`d1asha_`, `d1ashb_`, and others) useful for testing and tutorial purposes.

Example usage references these files to demonstrate core Foldseek functionality with minimal setup.

Sources: [example/1tim.pdb.gz:1-1](), [example/8tim.pdb.gz:1-1]()

# Summary Table of Common Commands

| Command                   | Purpose                                      | Input                           | Output                 |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------|---------------------------------|-----------------------|
| `foldseek easy-search`    | Search structures against database           | Structure files & DB dir        | Alignment results      |
| `foldseek easy-cluster`   | Cluster structures within a directory        | Directory with structures       | Cluster assignments    |
| `foldseek easy-multimersearch` | Multimer complex search                     | Complex structure files         | Complex alignment      |
| `foldseek databases`       | Download and prepare standard databases      | Datasetkey & output directory   | Foldseek-format DB     |
| `foldseek createdb`        | Create database from PDB/mmCIF/FASTA files   | Structure or sequence file(s)   | Indexed database       |
| `foldseek createindex`     | Build auxiliary index files for database     | Foldseek-format DB              | Index files            |

# Core Components

This page documents the foundational architectural elements of FoldSeek that enable its core functionality for protein structure search and analysis. These components provide the infrastructure upon which FoldSeek's workflows and algorithms operate.

## Architecture Overview

The core components of FoldSeek form an integrated system that enables efficient protein structure manipulation, search, and analysis by combining command dispatching, parameter management, specialized database handling, and output conversion.

### Diagram: Architecture Overview

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Core Framework"
        CommandSystem["foldseekCommands\n(src/FoldseekBase.cpp)"]
        ParameterSystem["LocalParameters\n(src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Management"
        DatabaseSystem["structcreatedb\n(src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp)"]
        CoordinateSystem["Coordinate16\n(src/commons/Coordinate16.h)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Structure Processing"
        StructureParsers["GemmiWrapper\n(src/strucclustutils/GemmiWrapper.cpp)"]
        PulchraWrapper["PulchraWrapper\n(src/strucclustutils/PulchraWrapper.cpp)"]
    end

    subgraph "Output & Visualization"
        OutputConversion["structureconvertalis\n(src/strucclustutils/structureconvertalis.cpp)"]
        StructTTY["StructTTYView\n(src/workflow/StructTTYView.cpp)"]
    end
    
    CommandSystem --> ParameterSystem
    CommandSystem --> DatabaseSystem

    ParameterSystem --> DatabaseSystem
    ParameterSystem --> StructureParsers
    
    DatabaseSystem --> CoordinateSystem
    
    StructureParsers --> PulchraWrapper
    DatabaseSystem --> OutputConversion
    DatabaseSystem --> StructTTY
```

Sources: [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:1-17](), [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:1-45](), [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:1-110](), [src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:4-40]()

---

## Command System

The **Command System** provides the command-line interface infrastructure enabling interaction with FoldSeek’s functionality. It manages command registration, parameter validation, dispatch, and execution.

Commands are centrally registered in the `foldseekCommands` vector defined in `src/FoldseekBase.cpp`. Each command specifies its name, associated execution function (e.g., `structcreatedb`), parameter set (`LocalParameters`), help text, and input/output type declarations [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:17-41]().

Commands are organized into categories such as `COMMAND_MAIN`, `COMMAND_EASY`, `COMMAND_SET`, and `COMMAND_HIDDEN` [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:18-95]().

### Diagram: Command Registration and Dispatch

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Command {
        +string name
        +void* execFunction
        +vector~MMseqsParameter*~ parameters
    }
    
    class foldseekCommands {
        +vector~Command~ foldseekCommands
    }
    
    class LocalParameters {
        +getLocalInstance()
    }
    
    foldseekCommands --> Command : "contains"
    Command --> LocalParameters : "uses"
```

For details, see [Command System](#2.1).

Sources: [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:17-100](), [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:18-30]()

---

## Parameter System

The **Parameter System** centralizes configuration management in FoldSeek via the `LocalParameters` class defined in `src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp` and `src/commons/LocalParameters.h`. This class extends the MMseqs2 `Parameters` base class to include FoldSeek-specific settings like `tmScoreThr`, `lddtThr`, `alignmentType`, and `coordStoreMode` [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:9-40]().

The parameter system uses a singleton pattern accessed via `LocalParameters::getLocalInstance()` and associates parameter groups with specific workflows and utilities [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:18-26]().

### Diagram: Parameter Inheritance

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Parameters {
        <<MMseqs2 Base>>
    }
    
    class LocalParameters {
        +float tmScoreThr
        +float lddtThr
        +int alignmentType
        +int coordStoreMode
        +getLocalInstance()
    }
    
    Parameters <|-- LocalParameters : "inherits"
```

For details, see [Parameter System](#2.2).

Sources: [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:1-45](), [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:18-166]()

---

## Database System and Structure Processing

The **Database System** manages the creation, storage, indexing, and querying of protein structural data using an extension of the MMseqs2 database format. Input structures (PDB, mmCIF, tar archives, FASTA, TSV) are parsed via `GemmiWrapper` [src/strucclustutils/GemmiWrapper.cpp](), processed using `PulchraWrapper` for missing atom reconstruction [src/strucclustutils/PulchraWrapper.cpp](), and stored across multi-file databases (`_seq` for amino acid sequences, `_ss` for 3Di structural sequences, and `_ca` for C-alpha coordinates) [src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp]() [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:28-35]().

Coordinates are stored compactly using `Coordinate16` [src/commons/Coordinate16.h]() supporting float or differential integer storage modes (`coordStoreMode`) [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:25]() [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:105-107]().

### Diagram: Database Creation Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["PDB/mmCIF/Fasta/TSV Files"] --> Gemmi["GemmiWrapper\n(src/strucclustutils/GemmiWrapper.cpp)"]
    Gemmi --> Pulchra["PulchraWrapper\n(src/strucclustutils/PulchraWrapper.cpp)"]
    Pulchra --> Encoder["StructureTo3Di Encoding"]
    Gemmi --> Coord["Coordinate16\n(src/commons/Coordinate16.h)"]
    Encoder --> DBWriter["structcreatedb\n(src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp)"]
    Coord --> DBWriter
    DBWriter --> FoldSeekDB["FoldSeek Database\n(_seq, _ss, _ca)"]
```

For details, see [Database System](#2.3).

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:4-50](), [src/commons/Coordinate16.h:7-79](), [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:18-40]()

---

## Output Conversion and Visualization

FoldSeek provides utilities to convert internal alignment results into user-facing formats and interactive visualizations. This includes `structureconvertalis` for BLAST tab, SAM, HTML, and superposed PDB outputs, `convert2pdb` for structure extraction, complex multimer reporting, an embedded JS report viewer, and `StructTTYView` (`structty`) for terminal-based structure visualization [src/workflow/StructTTYView.cpp]() [src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt:7-14]().

### Diagram: Output Conversion Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Results["Alignment Results DB"] --> Conv["structureconvertalis\n(src/strucclustutils/structureconvertalis.cpp)"]
    Conv --> Formats["Output Formats\n(BLAST tab, SAM, HTML, PDB Superposition)"]
    Results --> PDB["convert2pdb\n(src/strucclustutils/convert2pdb.cpp)"]
    Results --> TTY["StructTTYView\n(src/workflow/StructTTYView.cpp)"]
```

For details, see [Output Conversion and Visualization](#2.4).

Sources: [src/workflow/StructTTYView.cpp:1-21](), [src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt:1-29]()

# Page: Command System

# Command System

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [data/createinterfacedb.sh](data/createinterfacedb.sh)
- [data/structdatabases.sh](data/structdatabases.sh)
- [src/FoldseekBase.cpp](src/FoldseekBase.cpp)
- [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h](src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h)
- [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp](src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp)
- [src/commons/LocalParameters.h](src/commons/LocalParameters.h)
- [src/foldseek.cpp](src/foldseek.cpp)
- [src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp](src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp)
- [src/strucclustutils/createstructinterfacedb.cpp](src/strucclustutils/createstructinterfacedb.cpp)

</details>



This page documents the command system in FoldSeek, which handles the registration, dispatching, and execution of all commands within the application. The command system is the primary interface through which users interact with FoldSeek's functionality. For detailed information on parameters used by commands, see [Parameter System](#2.2).

## Overview

FoldSeek employs a command-based architecture where distinct commands represent core functionalities—such as database creation, structure searching, and clustering—invoked via its command-line interface (CLI). This modular organization enables flexible extension and integration of structural bioinformatics operations alongside MMseqs2 base commands.

At startup, FoldSeek initializes two main command registries defined in `src/foldseek.cpp` and `src/FoldseekBase.cpp`:

- **baseCommands**: The core MMseqs2 commands for generic sequence operations [src/foldseek.cpp:15-18]().
- **foldseekCommands**: FoldSeek-specific commands focused on structural tasks [src/foldseek.cpp:16-19]().

These registries are populated during program initialization and allow centralized dispatching of user instructions.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CLI["\"Command Line Interface\""] --> Parser["\"Command Parser\""]
    Parser --> Validator["\"Command Validator\""]
    Validator --> Dispatcher["\"Command Dispatcher\""]
    Dispatcher --> Implementation["\"Command Implementation\""]
    Implementation --> Parameters["LocalParameters"]
    Implementation --> Execution["Execution"]
    
    subgraph "Command Registration (src/foldseek.cpp)"
        Register["init()"]
        BaseCommands["baseCommands"]
        FoldseekCommands["foldseekCommands"]
        Register --> BaseCommands
        Register --> FoldseekCommands
    end
    
    Parser --> Register
```

Sources: [src/foldseek.cpp:15-21](), [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:1-16]()

## Command Structure

FoldSeek commands are encapsulated as `Command` objects defined in the MMseqs2 core. Each command includes:

- A **name** string (e.g., `"createdb"`, `"easy-search"`).
- A pointer to the **command execution function** declared in [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h:1-44]().
- A pointer to **local parameters** specific to the command (e.g., `&localPar.structurecreatedb`) defined in [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:1-166]().
- A **category** (e.g., `COMMAND_MAIN`, `COMMAND_EASY`).
- Description strings for help output.
- Citation keys for academic attribution (e.g., `CITATION_FOLDSEEK`, `CITATION_PROSTT5`).
- Database type validation info for input/output files using `DbValidator`.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Command {
        +string name
        +function_ptr function
        +vector~MMseqsParameter~* params
        +int category
        +string description
        +string examples
        +string author
        +string inputOutputInfo
        +int citations
        +vector~DbType~ databases
    }
    note for Command "Defined in MMseqs2 core"
```

Sources: [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:17-41]()

### Command Declaration Example

A representative example of a `Command` registration is the `createdb` command in [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:18-41](). It maps the command string `"createdb"` to the implementing function `structcreatedb` with associated parameters and usage documentation:

```cpp
{"createdb", structcreatedb, &localPar.structurecreatedb, COMMAND_MAIN,
  "Convert PDB/mmCIF/tar[.gz]/DB files or directory/TSV to a structure DB",
  "# Process multiple files\nfoldseek createdb examples/1tim.pdb.gz examples/8tim.pdb.gz DB\n...",
  "Martin Steinegger <martin.steinegger@snu.ac.kr>",
  "<i:directory|.tsv>|<i:PDB|mmCIF[.gz]|tar[.gz]|DB> ... <i:PDB|mmCIF[.gz]|tar|DB> <o:sequenceDB>",
  CITATION_FOLDSEEK | CITATION_PROSTT5, 
  {{"PDB|mmCIF[.gz]|stdin|tar[.gz]|DB", DbType::ACCESS_MODE_INPUT, DbType::NEED_DATA | DbType::VARIADIC, &DbValidator::flatfileStdinAndGeneric}, 
   {"sequenceDB", DbType::ACCESS_MODE_OUTPUT, DbType::NEED_DATA, &DbValidator::flatfile}}}
```

Sources: [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:18-41]()

## Command Categories

Commands in FoldSeek are categorized using integer constants (e.g., `COMMAND_MAIN`, `COMMAND_EASY`) to control help system organization and visibility. Within [src/foldseek.cpp:12-13](), the flags `hide_base_commands = true` and `hide_base_downloads = true` suppress MMseqs2 base commands and downloads from the foldseek CLI help output for a cleaner user interface focused on structural tools.

| Category         | Description                                  |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| `COMMAND_MAIN`   | Main FoldSeek tools (e.g., `createdb`, `search`)            |
| `COMMAND_EASY`   | Simplified “easy” workflows (e.g., `easy-search`, `easy-cluster`) |
| `COMMAND_SET`    | Database management/subsetting (e.g., `createsubdb`)       |
| `COMMAND_HIDDEN` | Internal or experimental utilities (e.g., `structureto3didescriptor`) |

Sources: [src/foldseek.cpp:12-13](), [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:17-100]()

## Command Hierarchy and Workflow Integration

FoldSeek structures commands both by abstraction level and function:

- **Easy Commands**: High-level simplified workflows such as `easy-search` and `easy-cluster` that wrap complex pipelines into user-friendly interfaces.
- **Core Commands**: Fundamental commands for database construction, indexing, searching, and clustering.
- **Implementation Functions**: The actual C++ functions performing the command logic, declared in [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h:1-44]().

Commands often internally invoke lower-level commands or workflows, enabling a layered architecture.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "User Interface Level"
        direction LR
        easy["\"Easy Commands\""]
        easy --> easySearch["easy-search"]
        easy --> easyCluster["easy-cluster"]
        easy --> easyMultimer["easy-multimersearch"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Command Level"
        direction LR
        core["\"Core Commands\""]
        core --> dbCommands["\"Database Commands\""]
        core --> searchCommands["\"Search Commands\""]
        
        dbCommands --> createdb["createdb"]
        dbCommands --> createsubdb["createsubdb"]
        
        searchCommands --> search["search"]
        searchCommands --> multimersearch["multimersearch"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Implementation Level"
        direction LR
        impl["\"Command Implementations\""]
        impl --> structcreatedb["structcreatedb()"]
        impl --> structuresearch["structuresearch()"]
        impl --> easystructuresearch["easystructuresearch()"]
    end
    
    easySearch --> easystructuresearch
    easystructuresearch -.-> search
    search --> structuresearch
    createdb --> structcreatedb
```

Sources: [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:17-100](), [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h:1-44]()

## Command Registration and Initialization

The main program entry, [src/foldseek.cpp:5-22](), handles command registration and initialization:

- `init()` is the central function called on startup to register commands, invoking `registerCommands` twice: once for the MMseqs2 `baseCommands` and once for FoldSeek-specific `foldseekCommands` [src/foldseek.cpp:17-20]().
- A global parameter singleton holding command parameters (`LocalParameters`) is instantiated via `initParameterSingleton()` [src/foldseek.cpp:22]().
- FoldSeek extends the database validator (`DbValidator`) in [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:9-15]() to support additional structural database types such as `DBTYPE_CA_ALPHA` and `DBTYPE_TMSCORE`, ensuring correct validation of structural databases.

```cpp
void init() {
    registerCommands(&baseCommands);
    registerCommands(&foldseekCommands);
}
void (*initCommands)(void) = init;

void initParameterSingleton() { 
    new LocalParameters; 
}
```

Flags are set to hide base MMseqs2 commands by default in [src/foldseek.cpp:12-13]():

```cpp
bool hide_base_commands = true;
bool hide_base_downloads = true;
```

Sources: [src/foldseek.cpp:5-22](), [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:8-15]()

## Shell Script Integration and Build Process

High-level workflows, such as those behind easy commands and database downloads, are implemented as shell scripts (e.g., [data/structdatabases.sh:1-178](), [data/createinterfacedb.sh:1-45]()). These scripts reside in the `data/` directory and are compiled into C++ header files via the MMseqsResourceCompiler during the build process. This enables runtime embedding and execution within the FoldSeek binary.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Build System (CMake)"
        SH["data/structdatabases.sh"] --> RC["MMseqsResourceCompiler"]
        RC --> H["structdatabases.sh.h"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Runtime"
        H --> FB["FoldseekBase.cpp"]
        FB --> Exec["\"Command Execution\""]
    end
```

During runtime, these embedded scripts orchestrate workflows such as database downloads, preprocessing, and cluster setups that are convenient to manage outside strict C++ code, as seen in `createinterfacedb` ([src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp:9-25]()).

Sources: [data/structdatabases.sh:1-178](), [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:1-6](), [src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp:9-25]()

## Available Commands Overview

FoldSeek exposes a broad suite of commands organized by their primary function:

| Category       | Command Examples                        | Source Reference             |
|----------------|---------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Database**   | `createdb`, `databases`, `createsubdb`| [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:17-60]() |
| **Search**     | `search`, `easy-search`, `multimersearch` | [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:61-100]() |
| **Clustering** | `cluster`, `easy-cluster`, `multimercluster` | [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h:1-44]() |
| **Utilities**  | `tmalign`, `convert2pdb`, `compressca` | [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h:12-23]() |

Each command consists of a function declared in [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h:1-44]() and defined in the source tree, and is registered with an associated parameter bundle in `foldseekCommands`.

Sources: [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:17-692](), [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h:1-44]()

---

This command system framework provides a scalable and extensible foundation for FoldSeek, enabling rapid development and integration of novel structural bioinformatics workflows while leveraging the robust MMseqs2 base infrastructure.

# Parameter System

The parameter system in Foldseek provides a comprehensive framework that defines, parses, validates, and provides access to command-line parameters and configuration options across the entire codebase. It is essential for managing user input, configuring workflows, and controlling output behaviors in structure search, alignment, clustering, multimer handling, and database management.

Sources:  
[src/commons/LocalParameters.h:18-26]()  
[src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:9-44]()  
[lib/mmseqs/src/commons/Parameters.h:21-61]()  
[lib/mmseqs/src/commons/Parameters.cpp:30-70]()

---

## Architectural Overview: Parameter Class Hierarchy

Foldseek’s parameter system extends the MMseqs2 parameter framework (`Parameters`) to include structure-specific options needed for protein structure analysis and comparison. It centralizes parameter definitions and groups, enforces validation regexes, and supports modular composition of workflow parameters.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Parameters {
        <<MMseqs2 Base>>
        +static Parameters* instance
        +parseParameters()
        +getInstance()
        +setDefaults()
        +std::map parameters
    }

    class LocalParameters {
        <<FoldSeek Extensions>>
        +getLocalInstance()
        +float tmScoreThr
        +int alignmentType
        +int coordStoreMode
        +std::vector~MMseqsParameter*~ structurecreatedb
        +std::vector~MMseqsParameter*~ tmalign
        +std::vector~MMseqsParameter*~ structurealign
    }

    class MMseqsParameter {
        <<Parameter Definition>>
        +const char* name
        +const char* description
        +unsigned int category
        +const std::type_info& type
        +const char* regex
        +bool wasSet
        +void* value
    }

    Parameters <|-- LocalParameters
    Parameters "1" *-- "many" MMseqsParameter : "contains"
```

- `Parameters` manages low-level parameter parsing and lifecycle [lib/mmseqs/src/commons/Parameters.h:66-67]().
- `LocalParameters` specializes and extends options specifically for Foldseek [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:18-26]().
- Each parameter is instantiated as an `MMseqsParameter` containing metadata and a pointer to the storage variable [lib/mmseqs/src/commons/Parameters.h:21-31]().

Sources:  
[src/commons/LocalParameters.h:18-26]()  
[lib/mmseqs/src/commons/Parameters.h:21-61]()  
[lib/mmseqs/src/commons/Parameters.cpp:30-70]()

---

## Parameter Definition and Storage

Parameters are defined in `LocalParameters::LocalParameters()` [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:9-40]() using `MMseqsParameter` descriptors. Each entry binds a command-line flag name, help text, data type (`typeid`), target member variable, validation regex, and category flags.

For example, the TM-score threshold parameter is defined as:

```cpp
PARAM_TMSCORE_THRESHOLD(
    PARAM_TMSCORE_THRESHOLD_ID,
    "--tmscore-threshold",
    "TMscore threshold",
    "accept alignments with a tmsore > thr [0.0,1.0]",
    typeid(float),
    (void*)&tmScoreThr,
    "^0(\\.[0-9]+)?|1(\\.0+)?$"
)
```

The underlying member variables (e.g., `tmScoreThr`, `alignmentType`, `coordStoreMode`) reside directly inside `LocalParameters` [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:9-40]() and are populated during command-line parsing.

Sources:  
[src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:9-40]()  
[lib/mmseqs/src/commons/Parameters.h:18-61]()

---

## Parameter Groups and Workflow Composition

Foldseek organizes parameters into logical groups represented by `std::vector<MMseqsParameter*>` [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:131-166](). These vectors aggregate parameters pertinent to specific sub-commands or multi-stage workflows.

### Diagram: Parameter Composition and Group Membership

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph MMseqsParameter Instances
        P1["PARAM_TMSCORE_THRESHOLD"]
        P2["PARAM_ALIGNMENT_TYPE"]
        P3["PARAM_COORD_STORE_MODE"]
        P4["PARAM_THREADS"]
    end

    subgraph Parameter Vectors in LocalParameters
        SALIGN["LocalParameters::structurealign"]
        SSEARCH["LocalParameters::structuresearchworkflow"]
        SDB["LocalParameters::structurecreatedb"]
    end

    P1 -->|assigned_to| SALIGN
    P2 -->|assigned_to| SALIGN
    P3 -->|assigned_to| SDB
    P4 -->|assigned_to| SSEARCH

    SALIGN -->|composed_into| SSEARCH
    LocalParameters["LocalParameters::getLocalInstance()"] --- SALIGN
    LocalParameters --- SSEARCH
    LocalParameters --- SDB
```

Workflows combine lower-level parameter vectors (such as `structurealign` and prefilter parameters) into composite vectors like `structuresearchworkflow` [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:133-135]().

Sources:  
[src/commons/LocalParameters.h:131-166]()  
[src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:9-40]()

---

## Parameter Flow and Lifecycle

The parameter lifecycle spans three main phases: singleton initialization, command-line parsing with regex validation, and runtime access.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as "User Command Line"
    participant Foldseek as "FoldseekBase.cpp"
    participant LocalPar as "LocalParameters::getLocalInstance()"
    participant BasePar as "Parameters::parseParameters()"

    User->>Foldseek: "foldseek easy-search query.pdb target/ res tmp"
    Foldseek->>LocalPar: "getLocalInstance()"
    LocalPar->>BasePar: "parseParameters(argc, argv)"
    BasePar->>BasePar: "Validate against MMseqsParameter.regex"
    BasePar-->>LocalPar: "Populate member variables (tmScoreThr, alignmentType, etc.)"
    LocalPar-->>Foldseek: "Parameters ready for workflow execution"
```

### Runtime Parameter Access Example
Throughout backend execution, code accesses parameters via the singleton instance:

```cpp
LocalParameters &par = LocalParameters::getLocalInstance();
if (par.alignmentType == LocalParameters::ALIGNMENT_TYPE_TMALIGN) {
    // Execute TM-align logic
}
```

[src/commons/LocalParameters.h:21-26]()  
[lib/mmseqs/src/commons/Parameters.h:44-48]()

## Parameter Categories and Visibility

Each `MMseqsParameter` instance contains a category bitmask governing help generation and visibility [lib/mmseqs/src/commons/Parameters.h:29-41]().

| Category Flag | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `COMMAND_COMMON` | Visible to standard users in regular help outputs. |
| `COMMAND_EXPERT` | Advanced options hidden by default; revealed with expert flags [lib/mmseqs/src/commons/Parameters.h:39](). |
| `COMMAND_HIDDEN` | Internal or deprecated backward-compatibility flags (e.g., `PARAM_MULTIMER_REPORT_MODE_BC_COMPAT`) [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:34](). |

</details>



The FoldSeek Database System forms the core foundation for storing, indexing, and managing protein structure data in formats optimized for fast similarity searching, clustering, and further structural analysis. This page thoroughly documents the internal design, data flow, and key components involved in database creation and management within FoldSeek. It is intended for technical readers requiring in-depth knowledge of the database subsystem implementation.

For usage examples related to databases, see the [Basic Usage Examples (#1.3)]() page, and for how databases integrate into search workflows, consult the [Structure Search (#3.1)]() page.

---

## 1. Overview of Database Organization

FoldSeek databases are organized as a set of interrelated files, each specialized to store certain features or metadata. This modular multicomponent format enables efficient access and selective loading of data needed for different search or clustering steps.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph FoldSeekMultiFileDatabase["FoldSeek Multi-file Database Format"]
        direction LR
        DB_MAIN["DBMain<basename>(sequences)"]
        DB_SS["DBSS(_ssDB_3Di_sequences)"]
        DB_CA["DBCA(_caDB_Calpha_coordinates)"]
        DB_H["DBH(_hDB_Headers_and_metadata)"]
        DB_MAP["DBMap(_idDB_Taxonomies_mappings)"]
        
        DB_MAIN --- DB_SS
        DB_MAIN --- DB_CA
        DB_MAIN --- DB_H
        DB_MAIN --- DB_MAP
    end

    subgraph FileExtensionsAndIndexing["File Extensions & Indexing"]
        suffixMain["SuffixMain(<basename>)"]
        suffixSS["SuffixSS(<basename>_ss)"]
        suffixCA["SuffixCA(<basename>_ca)"]
        suffixH["SuffixH(<basename>_h)"]
        suffixID["SuffixID(<basename>_id)"]

        suffixMain -.-> suffixMainType["<basename>.dbtype/.index"]
        suffixSS -.-> suffixSSType["<basename>_ss.dbtype/_ss.index"]
        suffixCA -.-> suffixCAType["<basename>_ca.dbtype/_ca.index"]
        suffixH -.-> suffixHType["<basename>_h.dbtype/_h.index"]
        suffixID -.-> suffixIDType["<basename>_id.dbtype/_id.index"]
    end
```

### Database Components

| File                     | Code Representation / Class | Role                                             |
|--------------------------|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| `<basename>`             | `DBReader`/`DBWriter`     | Amino acid sequences and main sequence database   |
| `<basename>_ss`          | `DBReader`/`DBWriter`     | 3Di structural alphabet sequences (`_ss`)         |
| `<basename>_ca`          | `Coordinate16`/`DBWriter` | Cα atomic coordinates (`_ca`, float/int16)        |
| `<basename>_h`           | `DBReader`                | Headers, metadata, descriptions (`_h`)            |
| `<basename>_id` (optional)| `DBReader`               | Taxonomy IDs and custom mappings (`_id`)          |

Each file has accompanying `.dbtype` and `.index` files that define its database type and support fast keyed access via `DBReader` and `DBWriter`.

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:442-494](), [src/strucclustutils/createstructsubdb.cpp:1-31]()

---

## 2. Database Creation Process (`structcreatedb`)

Database creation in FoldSeek primarily happens through the `createdb` command, implemented in the function `structcreatedb` (defined in `src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp`). This pipeline ingests raw structure or sequence files and outputs the multi-file database described above.

### Data Flow for `structcreatedb`

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    InputFiles["InputFiles(PDB/mmCIF/Fasta/tar/DBs)"] --> FormatDetect["GemmiWrapper::load / loadFromBuffer"]
    FormatDetect --> GemmiParse["GemmiWrapper(Parses structures)"]
    
    GemmiParse --> ChainExtract["ChainExtraction(readStructure.chain)"]
    
    subgraph FeatureExtraction["Feature Extraction Pipeline"]
        direction TB
        ChainExtract --> CoordinateExtract["CoordinateExtraction(ca, n, c, cb vectors)"]
        CoordinateExtract --> PulchraFix["PulchraWrapper(Fix missing atoms)"]
        PulchraFix --> To3Di["StructureTo3Di(Convert to 3Di sequences seq3di)"]
    end
    
    To3Di --> DataStore["DBWriter::writeData"]
    
    DataStore --> DB_AA["MainDB(Amino Acids)"]
    DataStore --> DB_3Di["SSDB(_ss 3Di Sequences)"]
    DataStore --> DB_CA["CADB(_ca Coordinates)"]
    DataStore --> DB_H["HDB(_h Headers)"]
    DataStore --> DB_MAP["IDDB(_id Optional Mapping)"]
```

### Input Formats Supported

- **Protein Structures:** PDB format, mmCIF format, mmJSON format, Foldcomp compressed format (`GemmiWrapper::Format`)
- **Sequence Files:** FASTA files used with the ProstT5 model for predicted 3Di sequences

FoldSeek can consume directories, tar archives (optionally gzipped via `structure_mtar_gzopen` or zstd via `mtar_zstdopen`), or even database files as input sources.

### Key Classes and Functions

- **`GemmiWrapper`**: Responsible for reading, parsing, and extracting structural information from input files. Supports multiple structure formats, including compressed files (`src/strucclustutils/GemmiWrapper.h:14-89]`, `src/strucclustutils/GemmiWrapper.cpp:30-188`).
- **`PulchraWrapper`**: Repairs missing atoms in structure data, particularly important for converting backbone-only structures into full Cα traces (`src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:228-280`).
- **`StructureTo3Di`**: Converts atomic coordinates into discrete 3Di alphabet sequences for downstream structural comparison.

### Database Writers

FoldSeek uses the generic templated `DBWriter` class to write each type of data component:
- Amino acid sequences are stored in the main database (`src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:442-455`).
- The 3Di sequences are stored in the `_ss` suffix database (`src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:456-470`).
- Cα coordinates are stored in the `_ca` suffix database, optionally compressed (`src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:471-490`).
- Headers and chain metadata in the `_h` suffix database (`src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:491-510`).

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:44-560](), [src/strucclustutils/GemmiWrapper.cpp:30-188](), [src/strucclustutils/GemmiWrapper.h:14-89]()

---

## 3. Coordinate Storage and Compression

FoldSeek supports different modes for storing Cα coordinates based on precision and compression trade-offs, controlled by the parameter `coordStoreMode`:

| Mode                        | Description                                         | Reference Classes/Code                          |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `COORD_STORE_MODE_CA_FLOAT` (1) | Store coordinates as raw floats (x,y,z)           | `DBWriter` writing float arrays [src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:490-530]() |
| `COORD_STORE_MODE_CA_DIFF` (2)  | Store coordinates as difference-encoded `int16_t` arrays | `Coordinate16::convertToDiff16` [src/commons/Coordinate16.h:7-80]() |
| `COORD_STORE_MODE_CA_PLAIN_TEXT` (3) | Store coordinates as plain text floating point numbers | [src/strucclustutils/compressca.cpp:13-122]() |

### `Coordinate16` Utility

The `Coordinate16` class is a utility used to convert full precision floating point coordinates into more compact difference-encoded 16-bit integers, reducing storage size and I/O bandwidth.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Coordinate16 {
        -float* buffer
        -size_t bufferSize
        +Coordinate16()
        +~Coordinate16()
        +float* read(const char* mem, size_t chainLength, size_t entryLength)
        +bool convertToDiff16(size_t len, T* data, int16_t* out, int stride)
    }
```

The encoding stores the first coordinate in full 32-bit integer form (`int32_t`) scaled by 1000 and then all subsequent values as signed 16-bit offsets (`int16_t`) from the prior coordinate, enabling substantial compression if atomic positions vary smoothly.

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:510-530](), [src/commons/Coordinate16.h:7-80](), [src/strucclustutils/compressca.cpp:13-122]()

---

## 4. Auxiliary Database Management and Utilities

### Creating Subdatabases (`createstructsubdb`)

FoldSeek supports creating subsets of existing databases for focused analysis through `createstructsubdb` (defined in `src/strucclustutils/createstructsubdb.cpp` and orchestrated via `data/createstructsubdb.sh`):

```mermaid
graph TD
    SubsetFile["IDListFile(LIST)"] --> CreateSubdb["MMseqs::createsubdb"]
    InputDB["InputDBFiles(IN)"] --> CreateSubdb
    CreateSubdb --> OutputDB["OutputSubsetDB(OUT)"]
    CreateSubdb --> IndexTmp["Sort Index .indextmp"]
    IndexTmp --> SubDBSs["createsubdb for _ss, _ca, _id"]
```

All major database components (`_ss`, `_ca`, `_h`, `_id`) are subset by mapping the list of keys to extract corresponding data efficiently, preserving internal index integrity.

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/createstructsubdb.cpp:1-31](), [data/createstructsubdb.sh:1-39]()

### Making Padded Databases for GPU (`makepaddedseqdb`)

To optimize sequence and structure databases for GPU-based searches, a padded sequence processing step is executed via `makepaddeddb` and `data/makepaddeddb.sh`:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    InDB["InputDB(IN)"] --> LNDB["MMseqs::lndb to prepare key mapping"]
    LNDB --> PadSeqDB["MMseqs::base:makepaddedseqdb"]
    PadSeqDB --> OutDB["OutputPaddedDB(OUT)"]

    RemapKeys["MMseqs::renamedbkeys to adjust mappings"] --> OutDB
```

This workflow normalizes sequence lengths with padding, generates lookup tables (`.gpu_mapping1`, `.gpu_mapping2`), and remaps database keys for accelerated GPU-based execution.

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/makepaddeddb.cpp:1-35](), [data/makepaddeddb.sh:1-174]()

### Index Creation (`structureindex`)

To accelerate database searches, FoldSeek creates indexing files that map keys and facilitate lookups via `structureindex` (`src/workflow/StructureIndex.cpp`) and `data/structureindex.sh`:

```mermaid
graph TD
    DB["TargetDB(DB)"] --> MMCreateIndex["MMseqs::mmcreateindex"]
    MMCreateIndex --> DBIdx["DB.idx index file"]
    MMCreateIndex --> SSIdx["DB_ss.idx"]
    MMCreateIndex --> HIdx["DB_ss_h.index"]
    MMCreateIndex --> CAIdx["AppendDBToIndex for _ca (optional)"]
```

Sources: [src/workflow/StructureIndex.cpp:1-73](), [data/structureindex.sh:1-56]()

## Purpose and Scope
This page details how Foldseek converts raw structural alignment results (stored in internal binary database formats containing alignments, backtraces, and 16-bit coordinate blocks) into user-facing output formats and visualization interfaces. Specifically, we examine the implementation of `structureconvertalis` output modes, `convert2pdb`, multimer report generators (`createmultimerreport`, `expandmultimer`), the embedded JavaScript web report viewer, and the `structty` terminal structure visualization subsystem backed by `lib/structty`.

---

## 1. Alignment Result Conversion via `structureconvertalis`
The core conversion utility in Foldseek is `structureconvertalis` [src/strucclustutils/structureconvertalis.cpp:1](), which reads alignment result databases and translates them into various human-readable or downstream-compatible file formats based on parameter flags.

### Supported Output Modes
`structureconvertalis` supports multiple output formats:
- **BLAST-tab / Custom Tabular (`--format-output`)**: Detailed column-based text output containing query and target identifiers, E-values, bit scores, sequence identity, coverage fractions, and full-length alignment summaries [src/strucclustutils/structureconvertalis.cpp:171-205]().
- **SAM Format**: Converts structural alignment backtraces into standard Sequence Alignment/Map (SAM) format records for compatibility with genomics pipelines.
- **HTML Report (`--format-mode 3`)**: Generates an interactive self-contained HTML page embedding the alignment viewer and 3Di/amino acid sequence alignments [src/strucclustutils/structureconvertalis.cpp:20]() (utilizing `main.js.h` and `vendor.js.zst.h`).
- **Superposed PDB (`--format-mode 2` or similar)**: Applies the rotation matrix $U$ and translation vector $t$ computed during TM-align or superposition steps to transform target coordinates onto the query frame, outputting superposed PDB/mmCIF structures.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Raw Alignment DB (db3)"] --> B["structureconvertalis (src/strucclustutils/structureconvertalis.cpp)"]
    B --> C["BLAST Tabular Output"]
    B --> D["SAM Format"]
    B --> E["Interactive HTML Report (main.js.h)"]
    B --> F["Superposed PDB / mmCIF"]

    sub:Sources["Sources: src/strucclustutils/structureconvertalis.cpp"]
```
*Sources: [src/strucclustutils/structureconvertalis.cpp:1]()*

---

## 2. Structure Coordinate Conversion via `convert2pdb`
The `convert2pdb` tool [src/strucclustutils/convert2pdb.cpp:77]() transforms Foldseek's compressed binary structure databases (`_ca`, `_ca.index`, `.lookup`) back into standard PDB or mmCIF coordinate files.

### Key Implementation Details
- **Output Modes**: Controlled via `par.pdbOutputMode` [src/strucclustutils/convert2pdb.cpp:81](), supporting single-chain outputs, complex groupings [src/strucclustutils/convert2pdb.cpp:112](), and multi-model files (`PDB_OUTPUT_MODE_MULTIMODEL`) [src/strucclustutils/convert2pdb.cpp:120]().
- **Format Selection**: Supports both traditional PDB format and mmCIF format (`pdbOutputFormat`) via Gemmi wrappers (`GemmiWriter`) [src/strucclustutils/convert2pdb.cpp:82-85, 118]().
- **Coordinate Decoding**: Reads 16-bit coordinate blocks using `Coordinate16` [src/strucclustutils/convert2pdb.cpp:162]() and reconstructs full atom records, applying standard three-letter amino acid code lookups [src/strucclustutils/convert2pdb.cpp:145]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Foldseek DB (.db1, _ca)"] --> B["convert2pdb (src/strucclustutils/convert2pdb.cpp)"]
    B --> C["KeyIterator / MapIterator"]
    C --> D["GemmiWriter / Coordinate16"]
    D --> E["PDB Files or mmCIF Files"]

    sub:Sources["Sources: src/strucclustutils/convert2pdb.cpp"]
```
*Sources: [src/strucclustutils/convert2pdb.cpp:1-176]()*

---

## 3. Multimer Reports and Complex Scoring
For multi-chain protein complexes and multimers, Foldseek coordinates specialized reporting and expansion workflows to aggregate chain-to-chain alignments into complex-level metrics.

### Key Components
- **`scoremultimer`**: Computes complex TM-scores and interface metrics by combining individual chain superpositions and evaluating residue-residue distance matrices across complex interfaces (`INTERFACE_THRESHOLD = 8`) [src/strucclustutils/scoremultimer.cpp:1-20, 125]().
- **`createmultimerreport`**: Parses complex alignment databases and formats comprehensive summary tables mapping query complex identifiers to target complex identifiers, chain mappings, and TM-score vectors [src/strucclustutils/createmultimerreport.cpp:25-65]().
- **`expandmultimer`**: Expands chain-level search results into complex-level result databases by cross-referencing `.lookup` files for query and target databases [src/strucclustutils/expandmultimer.cpp:27-70]().
- **`aln2tmscore`**: Re-scores structural alignments by recalculating exact TM-scores from $C_\alpha$ coordinates and transformation matrices [src/strucclustutils/aln2tmscore.cpp:17-106]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Chain Alignments (db3)"] --> B["expandmultimer (src/strucclustutils/expandmultimer.cpp)"]
    B --> C["scoremultimer (src/strucclustutils/scoremultimer.cpp)"]
    C --> D["aln2tmscore (src/strucclustutils/aln2tmscore.cpp)"]
    D --> E["createmultimerreport (src/strucclustutils/createmultimerreport.cpp)"]
    E --> F["Multimer Report DB"]

    sub:Sources["Sources: src/strucclustutils/scoremultimer.cpp, src/strucclustutils/createmultimerreport.cpp, src/strucclustutils/expandmultimer.cpp, src/strucclustutils/aln2tmscore.cpp"]
```
*Sources: [src/strucclustutils/scoremultimer.cpp:1](), [src/strucclustutils/createmultimerreport.cpp:1](), [src/strucclustutils/expandmultimer.cpp:27](), [src/strucclustutils/aln2tmscore.cpp:17]()*

---

## 4. Embedded JavaScript Web Report Viewer
When HTML output mode is selected, Foldseek embeds a fully interactive client-side web application directly into the binary via CMake resource compilation.

### Implementation Architecture
- **Source Assets**: The frontend code is written in JavaScript (`data/main.js` [data/main.js:1]()) and bundled with dependencies compressed via Zstd (`data/vendor.js.zst` [data/vendor.js.zst:1]()).
- **Header Embedding**: During the build system resource compilation phase, these files are converted into C headers (`main.js.h`, `vendor.js.zst.h`) and included directly in `structureconvertalis.cpp` [src/strucclustutils/structureconvertalis.cpp:20-21]().
- **Client Features**: The embedded app provides interactive sequence alignment visualization, structure rendering bindings, metadata cards, and direct citation links [data/main.js:8-18]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Frontend Assets (data/main.js, data/vendor.js.zst)"] --> B["CMake Resource Compilation"]
    B --> C["C Headers (main.js.h, vendor.js.zst.h)"]
    C --> D["structureconvertalis (src/strucclustutils/structureconvertalis.cpp)"]
    D --> E["Self-Contained HTML Output Report"]

    sub:Sources["Sources: src/strucclustutils/structureconvertalis.cpp, data/main.js, data/vendor.js.zst"]
```
*Sources: [src/strucclustutils/structureconvertalis.cpp:20-21](), [data/main.js:1](), [data/vendor.js.zst:1]()*

---

## 5. StrucTTY Terminal Structure Viewer
Foldseek includes a terminal-based structure visualization utility (`structty`) powered by the vendored library `lib/structty`.

### Key Components & Data Flow
- **Command Entrypoint**: The `structty` command exposes terminal-based structure inspection directly in the CLI.
- **Database Integration**: Utilizes `FoldseekDBReader.cpp` [lib/structty/src/structure/FoldseekDBReader.cpp:1]() from `lib/structty` to read Foldseek databases (`_ca`, headers) directly without requiring external conversion tools.
- **Rendering Engine**: Leverages `lib/structty/include/structty.h` and `structty_render.h` to render ASCII/ANSI terminal graphics representing 3D protein backbone structures and chains.
- **Third-Party Dependencies**: Relies on Gemmi for coordinate parsing and stb image write utilities [lib/structty/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:5-18]().

# Page: Workflows

# Workflows

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [data/CMakeLists.txt](data/CMakeLists.txt)
- [data/structureiterativesearch.sh](data/structureiterativesearch.sh)
- [data/structureprofile.sh](data/structureprofile.sh)

- [src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt](src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt)
- [src/workflow/CMakeLists.txt](src/workflow/CMakeLists.txt)
- [src/workflow/StructureSearch.cpp](src/workflow/StructureSearch.cpp)

</details>



This page provides a high-level overview of the principal workflows implemented in FoldSeek. These workflows form the backbone of FoldSeek’s capabilities, enabling structural search, clustering, multimer processing, protein-protein interface analysis, and easy-to-use command interfaces. Each workflow combines various algorithmic components and auxiliary tools into multi-step pipelines managed by C++ controllers and shell script orchestrations.

For detailed step-by-step descriptions, parameter explanations, and command usage, please refer to the respective child pages linked below.

---

## Workflow Architecture and Execution Model

FoldSeek's workflow system integrates core C++ controllers, shell script templates compiled into binary headers, and a centralized parameter management system. Workflows are invoked via dedicated controllers (such as `structuresearch` in `[src/workflow/StructureSearch.cpp]()-30`) which parse user arguments using `LocalParameters` (`[src/workflow/StructureSearch.cpp]()-31`), set up temporary working directories, and configure script variables using `CommandCaller` (`[src/workflow/StructureSearch.cpp]()-89-98`).

```mermaid

        is["interfacesearch\n[src/workflow/InterfaceSearch.cpp]()"]
        es["easy-search\n[src/workflow/EasyStructureSearch.cpp]()"]
    end

    subgraph "Parameter & Dispatch System"
        params["LocalParameters\n[src/workflow/StructureSearch.cpp:31]()"]
        caller["CommandCaller\n[src/workflow/StructureSearch.cpp:89]()"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space: Shell Scripts"
        sh1["structuresearch.sh\n[data/structuresearch.sh:1-162]()"]
        sh2["structureiterativesearch.sh\n[data/structureiterativesearch.sh:1-149]()"]
        sh3["multimersearch.sh\n[data/data/CMakeLists.txt:21]()"]
        sh4["interfacesearch.sh\n[data/data/CMakeLists.txt:27]()"]
    end

    ss --> params
    sc --> params
    ms --> params
    is --> params
    es --> params

    params --> caller
    caller --> sh1
    caller --> sh2
    caller --> sh3

```

**Sources:**  
[src/workflow/StructureSearch.cpp:30-153]()
