## Purpose and Overview

The 3Di representation is a core component of FoldSeek that converts complex 3D protein structures into 1D sequences of categorical states encoding local structural environments. This maps structural comparison onto efficient sequence alignment algorithms. This page details the encoder neural network in `lib/3di`, the `mat3di` substitution matrix, `kerasify` inference mechanics, descriptor generation via `structureto3didescriptor`, backbone reconstruction using Pulchra, and spatial coordinate compression via `Coordinate16`.

Sources: [lib/3di/structureto3di.h:1-136](), [src/strucclustutils/structureto3didescriptor.cpp:22-163](), [src/commons/Coordinate16.h:7-79]()

## Core Concepts

The 3Di structural alphabet maps the local 3D neighborhood of each amino acid into a single letter from a 20-letter alphabet through geometric feature extraction, neural network projection, and discretization.

### Code-to-Logic Mapping: 3Di Generation

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        L1["Coordinate Loading"]
        L2["Backbone Reconstruction"]
        L3["Virtual Center Mapping"]
        L4["Neighbor Partner Finding"]
        L5["Geometric Feature Extraction"]
        L6["Neural Network Inference"]
        L7["Centroid Discretization"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        C1["GemmiWrapper::load"]
        C2["PulchraWrapper::rebuildBackbone"]
        C3["StructureTo3DiBase::replaceCBWithVirtualCenter"]
        C4["StructureTo3DiBase::findResiduePartners"]
        C5["StructureTo3Di::calcFeatures"]
        C6["KerasModel::Apply"]
        C7["StructureTo3Di::discretizeEmbeddings"]
    end

    L1 --- C1
    L2 --- C2
    L3 --- C3
    L4 --- C4
    L5 --- C5
    L6 --- C6
    L7 --- C7

    C1 --> C2 --> C3 --> C4 --> C5 --> C6 --> C7
```

Sources: [lib/3di/structureto3di.h:78-136](), [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:161-285](), [src/strucclustutils/structureto3didescriptor.cpp:73-136](), [lib/pulchra/pulchra.cpp:71-246]()

## 3Di Computation Algorithm

The conversion pipeline executed by `StructureTo3Di` involves several distinct processing stages:

### 1. Backbone Reconstruction

When input files lack full backbone coordinates (e.g., C-alpha only models), `PulchraWrapper::rebuildBackbone` reconstructs missing $N$ and $C$ atom positions based on C-alpha chains [src/strucclustutils/structureto3didescriptor.cpp:105-118]().

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/structureto3didescriptor.cpp:105-118](), [lib/pulchra/pulchra.cpp:71-246]()

### 2. Virtual Center Creation

Beta-carbon ($C_\beta$) positions (or virtual centers replacing them) are computed to standardize spatial orientation using `approxCBetaPosition` [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:49-67]() and `calcVirtualCenter` [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:73-99]().

Sources: [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:108-122](), [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:49-67](), [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:73-99]()

### 3. Residue Partner Identification

The algorithm searches for the spatially closest neighboring virtual center for each residue via `findResiduePartners` [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:136-157]().

Sources: [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:136-157]()

### 4. Feature Calculation

For each valid residue pair, a 10-dimensional feature vector (`Alphabet3Di::FEATURE_CNT`) is computed in `calcFeatures` [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:168-187]() capturing unit vector dot products and sequence separation metrics [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:184-185]().

Sources: [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:168-187](), [lib/3di/structureto3di.h:12]()

### 5. Neural Network Inference via Kerasify

The 10D feature vector is evaluated by a feed-forward neural network loaded via the lightweight `KerasModel` container [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:161-165](). Weights are compiled from `encoder_weights_3di.kerasify` [data/keras_weights_3di.kerasify]() into a 2D embedding space (`Alphabet3Di::EMBEDDING_DIM`) [lib/3di/structureto3di.h:13]().

Sources: [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:217-231](), [lib/3di/structureto3di.h:13]()

### 6. Discretization

The 2D embedding coordinates are mapped to the nearest of 20 predefined cluster centroids (`Alphabet3Di::centroids`) [lib/3di/structureto3di.h:18-39](), assigning a discrete 3Di state character.

Sources: [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:233-255](), [lib/3di/structureto3di.h:18-39]()

Sources: [lib/3di/structureto3di.h:78-136](), [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:1-285]()

## 3Di Substitution Matrix

Scoring between 3Di sequences relies on the `mat3di` substitution matrix loaded from `mat3di.out` [data/mat3di.out:1-25]().

| Property | Value / Detail |
|----------|----------------|
| Dimensions | $21 \times 21$ (20 states + 'X') |
| Score Range | -17 to +10 [data/mat3di.out:5-24]() |
| Scale Lambda | 0.351568 [data/mat3di.out:3]() |

Sources: [data/mat3di.out:1-25](), [src/strucclustutils/structureto3didescriptor.cpp:58]()

## Coordinate Compression (`Coordinate16`)

To minimize storage overhead for coordinate-heavy databases, FoldSeek compresses 3D float coordinates into 16-bit integer differential formats using `Coordinate16` [src/commons/Coordinate16.h:7-79]().

### Code-to-Logic Mapping: Coordinate Compression

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        L1["Float Coordinate Array"]
        L2["Absolute Start Scaling"]
        L3["Differential Integer Calculation"]
        L4["Buffer Management & Reallocation"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        C1["Coordinate16::convertToDiff16"]
        C2["memcpy (int32_t start)"]
        C3["__builtin_sub_overflow"]
        C4["Coordinate16::read"]
    end

    L1 --- C1
    L2 --- C2
    L3 --- C3
    L4 --- C4

    C1 --> C2 --> C3 --> C4
```

`Coordinate16::convertToDiff16` scales floating-point coordinates by $1000.0$, stores the absolute start as an `int32_t`, and encodes subsequent steps as 16-bit differences (`int16_t`) with overflow detection [src/commons/Coordinate16.h:60-74](). `Coordinate16::read` decodes this representation back into floating-point buffers dynamically [src/commons/Coordinate16.h:15-57]().

Sources: [src/commons/Coordinate16.h:7-79]()

        B -- "Ca-only" --> P["PulchraWrapper"]
        P --> C
    end

    subgraph "Database & Search"
        D --> E["Coordinate16 Storage"]

# Page: Protein Language Models

# Protein Language Models

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/strucclustutils/GemmiWrapper.cpp](src/strucclustutils/GemmiWrapper.cpp)
- [src/strucclustutils/GemmiWrapper.h](src/strucclustutils/GemmiWrapper.h)
- [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp](src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp)
- [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.h](src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.h)
- [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5ForkRunner.h](src/strucclustutils/ProstT5ForkRunner.h)
- [src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp](src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp)
- [util/update_prostt5.sh](util/update_prostt5.sh)

</details>



This page describes how protein language models are integrated into FoldSeek, with a focus on the `ProstT5` model implementation located in `src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp` and `src/strucclustutils/ProstT5ForkRunner.h`. Protein language models enhance FoldSeek's structural search capabilities by predicting structural features (3Di sequences) directly from amino acid sequences. For information on the complementary 3Di structural representation, see [3Di Representation](4.3).

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:1-231](), [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5ForkRunner.h:1-160]()

## Overview of Protein Language Models in FoldSeek

Protein Language Models (PLMs) are machine learning models trained on large sequence databases to capture sequence patterns. FoldSeek integrates the **ProstT5** model via a customized `llama.cpp` backend (`lib/prostt5`) to translate amino acid sequences into 3Di structural alphabet sequences during database creation.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "NaturalLanguageSpace"
        input["Protein Structures / Sequences"]
    end

    subgraph "CodeEntitySpace"
        input --> structcreatedb["structcreatedb.cpp"]
        structcreatedb --> regular["Regular DB Handling"]
        structcreatedb --> plm["prostt5Forking() [ProstT5ForkRunner.h]"]
        regular --> db_ca["_ca (Coordinates)"]
        regular --> db_h["_h (Headers)"]
        plm --> db_ss["_ss (3Di Predictions via ProstT5)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "SearchWorkflow"
        db_ca --> searchCmd["StructureSearch.cpp"]
        db_ss --> searchCmd
        db_h --> searchCmd
        searchCmd --> results["Alignment Results"]
    end
```
*Figure 1: Bridging natural language database creation concepts to C++ code entities in `structcreatedb.cpp` and `ProstT5ForkRunner.h`.*

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:20-29](), [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5ForkRunner.h:23-32]()

## ProstT5 Architecture

ProstT5 is implemented as a C++ wrapper around the `llama.cpp` inference engine. The integration relies on three primary C++ classes defined in `src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.h` and implemented in `src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp`.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class LlamaInitGuard {
        +LlamaInitGuard(verbose)
        +~LlamaInitGuard()
    }
    
    class ProstT5Model {
        +llama_model* model
        +ProstT5Model(model_file, device)
        +~ProstT5Model()
    }
    
    class ProstT5 {
        +ProstT5Model& model
        +llama_context* ctx
        +ProstT5(model, threads)
        +~ProstT5()
        +predict(aa) string
        +getDevices() vector~string~
    }
    
    LlamaInitGuard ..> ProstT5Model : "llama_backend_init()"
    ProstT5 --> ProstT5Model : "references"
    ProstT5 ..> llama_context : "manages lifecycle via llama_new_context_with_model()"
```
*Figure 2: Class hierarchy for ProstT5 inference within the code entity space.*

### Key Components

1.  **`LlamaInitGuard`**: Manages the global state of the underlying LLAMA backend. Its constructor calls `llama_backend_init()` and `llama_numa_init(GGML_NUMA_STRATEGY_DISABLED)`, while its destructor invokes `llama_backend_free()` [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:116-126]().
2.  **`ProstT5Model`**: Loads model weights from disk via `llama_load_model_from_file()` using configuration parameters parsed through `parse_device_list()` [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:81-148]().
3.  **`ProstT5`**: Allocates and manages the `llama_context` with non-causal attention (`GGML_BACKEND_DEVICE_TYPE_GPU` or CPU threads) and provides the `predict(const std::string& aa)` method [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:167-191]().

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.h:10-39](), [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:81-191]()

## Prediction Workflow

The prediction pipeline transforms raw amino acid sequences into structural 3Di sequences using the following procedure inside `ProstT5::predict`:

1.  **Tokenization**: Iterates through the input amino acid string, prepends a special symbol `▁` to each character (e.g., `▁A`, `▁C`), and maps unknown residues to the fallback token `▁X` via `llama_token_get_token()` [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:198-208]().
2.  **Prompting**: Prepends the special task token `<AA2fold>` to the tokenized sequence [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:197]().
3.  **Inference**: Invokes `llama_encode()` using batches constructed via `llama_batch_get_one()` [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:34-40]().
4.  **Decoding**: Extracts sequence embeddings via `llama_get_embeddings()`, performs an `argmax` operation over the first 20 dimensions (representing structural states), and maps indices to characters via `number_to_char()` [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:8-64]().

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:8-65](), [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:193-212]()

## Performance Optimizations

### Sequence Splitting for Long Proteins
ProstT5 operates under a fixed attention window constraint (default maximum context length of 2048 tokens). In `src/strucclustutils/ProstT5ForkRunner.h`, sequences exceeding `split_length` are partitioned into overlapping chunks. The overlapping bounds are dynamically adjusted using `minSplitLength`, and the individual chunk predictions are concatenated to form the complete 3Di sequence [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5ForkRunner.h:84-106]().

### CPU Inference via `prostt5Forking`
To maximize multi-core CPU throughput and prevent deadlocks or threading conflicts between OpenMP and `llama.cpp`, FoldSeek implements a multi-process fork runner (`prostt5Forking`):

*   **Process Management**: Sets `omp_set_num_threads(1)` to disable nested OpenMP threads, creates a System V message queue (`msgget`), and forks worker subprocesses [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5ForkRunner.h:33-52]().
*   **Work Distribution**: The parent process dispatches task indices (`TaskMsg`) via `msgsnd()`, while workers consume tasks via `msgrcv()` [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5ForkRunner.h:69-74, 128-134]().
*   **Isolation**: Each worker initializes its own `ProstT5Model` and `ProstT5` inference context, processes sequences, writes results to a thread-local temporary database using `DBWriter`, and exits via `_Exit(0)` [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5ForkRunner.h:59-119]().
*   **Result Merging**: The parent process waits for all worker processes to finish using `waitpid()` and merges temporary databases via `DBWriter::mergeResults()` [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5ForkRunner.h:141-159]().

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5ForkRunner.h:18-160]()

### GPU Acceleration
Device configuration is managed by `parse_device_list()`, which interprets comma-separated device identifiers against `ggml_backend_dev_by_name()` [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:81-101](). When valid GPU devices are detected, `ProstT5Model` sets `mparams.n_gpu_layers = 24` to offload model weights to the accelerator [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:130-146]().

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:81-101](), [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp:130-146]()

## Integration with Database Creation

The `structcreatedb` command orchestrates structure parsing, coordinate compression, and language model inference:

| Step | Implementation Function / Class | File Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Structure Parsing** | `GemmiWrapper::load()` / `loadFromBuffer()` | [src/strucclustutils/GemmiWrapper.h:39-53]() |
| **Coordinate Compression** | `Coordinate16` delta encoding | [src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:16]() |
| **PLM Execution** | `prostt5Forking()` (when `HAVE_PROSTT5` is defined) | [src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:20-29]() |
| **Result Storage** | `DBWriter` writing predictions to the `_ss` database | [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5ForkRunner.h:67-112]() |

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/structcreatedb.cpp:10-29](), [src/strucclustutils/GemmiWrapper.h:39-53](), [src/strucclustutils/ProstT5ForkRunner.h:67-112]()

# Developer Guide

<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

This page provides high-level information for developers who want to extend or modify FoldSeek. It covers the build system, Docker/CI environment, testing framework, adding new commands, and vendored libraries.

For information on using FoldSeek, see [Overview](#1) and [Basic Usage Examples](#1.3). For architectural details of core components, see [Core Components](#2).

## Build System

FoldSeek uses a CMake-based build system that integrates multiple internal modules and third-party libraries [CMakeLists.txt:1-8](). The top-level `CMakeLists.txt` manages global configuration flags (such as SIMD levels, CUDA support, and static linking options), submodule initialization, and target compilation [CMakeLists.txt:1-118]().

**System Component Map**
```mermaid
graph TD
    ROOT["CMakeLists.txt"] --> SRC["src/CMakeLists.txt"]
    ROOT --> DATA["data/CMakeLists.txt"]
    ROOT --> MMSEQS["lib/mmseqs"]
    ROOT --> T3DI["lib/3di"]
    ROOT --> KERAS["lib/kerasify"]
    ROOT --> TMAL["lib/tmalign"]
    ROOT --> PROST["lib/prostt5"]
    SRC --> WFLOW["src/workflow"]
    SRC --> UTILS["src/strucclustutils"]
    SRC --> COMM["src/commons"]
```
Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:34-118](), [src/CMakeLists.txt:3-6](), [data/CMakeLists.txt:1-33]()

For details on CMake targets, submodule management, resource embedding, and compiler flags, see [Build System](#5.1).

## CI and Docker Environment

Automated builds and testing are orchestrated via Azure Pipelines [azure-pipelines.yml:1-10]() and GitHub Actions workflows. FoldSeek provides multi-architecture Docker environments for Linux (including manylinux-based GPU containers) [azure-pipelines.yml:91-96]() and cross-compilation toolchains [azure-pipelines.yml:114-116]() to ensure consistent binary generation and static linking compliance.

Sources: [azure-pipelines.yml:1-182](), [.github/workflows/Dockerfile.GPU-manylinux2014:1-35]()

For details on Dockerfiles, CI matrix configurations, universal macOS builds, and artifact publishing, see [CI and Docker Environment](#5.2).

## Testing Framework

FoldSeek uses a regression test suite anchored by `run_regression.sh` [azure-pipelines.yml:75-75]() and example files located in the `examples/` directory. CI pipelines run these tests across various SIMD configurations and sanitizers (such as AddressSanitizer) to catch memory issues and behavioral regressions [azure-pipelines.yml:37-41]().

Sources: [azure-pipelines.yml:37-77]()

For details on running regression tests, test data organization, and parameter sampling utilities like `samplemulambda`, see [Testing Framework](#5.3).

## Adding New Commands

Extending FoldSeek with new commands or workflows involves declaring the entry point in `LocalCommandDeclarations.h`, registering the command handler in `FoldseekBase.cpp` [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:17-96](), defining parameters in `LocalParameters`, creating workflow shell scripts in `data/`, and wiring them into resource compilation via `data/CMakeLists.txt` [data/CMakeLists.txt:3-25]().

**Command to Code Entity Mapping**
```mermaid
graph TD
    EXE["foldseek.cpp"] --> BASE["FoldseekBase.cpp"]
    BASE --> C1["createdb"]
    BASE --> C2["easy-search"]
    BASE --> C3["search"]
    BASE --> C4["easy-cluster"]
    C1 --- F1["structcreatedb"]
    C2 --- F2["easystructuresearch"]
    C3 --- F3["structuresearch"]
    C4 --- F4["easystructurecluster"]
```
Sources: [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:17-96](), [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h:1-35]()

For a complete step-by-step developer guide, see [Adding New Commands](#5.4).

## Vendored Libraries

FoldSeek bundles several third-party libraries under `lib/` to handle specific domains, such as the MMseqs2 framework, `gemmi` for structure parsing, `foldcomp`, `tmalign`, `pulchra`, `kerasify`, `3di`, `prostt5`/`ggml`, and `structty` [CMakeLists.txt:9-58](). Each library is integrated via CMake subdirectories or custom update scripts.

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:9-62]()

For details on each vendored library and its integration approach, see [Vendored Libraries](#5.5).

# Build System

## Purpose and Overview

This document describes the build system used by FoldSeek, a tool for fast and sensitive structural searches of protein structures. The build system is based on CMake and manages a complex dependency tree including submodules, resource compilation for neural network weights and shell scripts, and specialized SIMD/GPU/StrucTTY build flags.

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:1-118]()

## Build System Architecture

FoldSeek's build process is centered around a hierarchical CMake structure that integrates the core MMseqs2 framework (`lib/mmseqs`) with FoldSeek-specific structural alignment and scoring modules (`src/commons`, `src/strucclustutils`, `src/workflow`).

### Build Orchestration and Code Entity Mapping

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Resource Generation [data/CMakeLists.txt]"
        RC["compile_resource()"]
        DATA["data/CMakeLists.txt"]
        SH["structuresearch.sh"]
        KERAS["encoder_weights_3di.kerasify"]
        RC --> DATA
        SH --> DATA
        KERAS --> DATA
        DATA --> HEADERS["local-generated Headers"]
    end

    subgraph "Core Library [src/CMakeLists.txt]"
        direction TB
        COMM["src/commons"]
        STRU["src/strucclustutils"]
        WORK["src/workflow"]
        BASE["FoldseekBase.cpp"]
        
        COMM --> FF["foldseek-framework"]
        STRU --> FF
        WORK --> FF
        BASE --> FF
    end

    subgraph "Executable Target [src/CMakeLists.txt]"
        FS_EXE["foldseek"]
    end

    HEADERS --> FF
    FF --> FS_EXE
```

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:33-46](), [src/CMakeLists.txt:8-50](), [data/CMakeLists.txt:1-39]()

### Build Targets and Entity Mapping

The following table maps logical system components to their specific code implementations and CMake targets.

| Component | CMake Target | Source Directory | Primary Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Command Registry** | `foldseek-framework` | `src/FoldseekBase.cpp` | Registers all `foldseekCommands` [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:1-120]() |
| **PDB/mmCIF Parser** | `gemmiwrapper` | `src/strucclustutils/GemmiWrapper.cpp` | Wraps Gemmi and Foldcomp for structure IO [src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt:31-50]() |
| **3Di Encoding** | `3di` | `lib/3di` | Implements the 3Di alphabet and state transitions [CMakeLists.txt:41]() |
| **NN Inference** | `kerasify` | `lib/kerasify` | CPU-based inference for 3Di and E-value networks [CMakeLists.txt:43]() |
| **Language Model** | `prostt5` | `src/strucclustutils/ProstT5.cpp` | Integration with `ggml` for 3Di prediction [src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt:51-54]() |
| **Terminal Viewer** | `structty` | `lib/structty` | Terminal structure visualization workflow [CMakeLists.txt:47-62](), [src/workflow/CMakeLists.txt:19]() |

Sources: [src/CMakeLists.txt:8-50](), [src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt:1-54](), [src/workflow/CMakeLists.txt:1-21]()

## Resource Compilation

FoldSeek embeds shell scripts, substitution matrices, and neural network weights directly into the binary to ensure portability. This is handled by `MMseqsResourceCompiler` included in `data/CMakeLists.txt`.

1. **Input**: Files such as `structuresearch.sh` [data/CMakeLists.txt:8](), `mat3di.out` [data/CMakeLists.txt:13](), and `encoder_weights_3di.kerasify` [data/CMakeLists.txt:14]().
2. **Process**: The `compile_resource` function transforms these files into C++ headers [data/CMakeLists.txt:33-37]().
3. **Dependency**: The `foldseek-framework` target depends on `local-generated` via `add_dependencies` to ensure headers are ready before compilation [src/CMakeLists.txt:33]().
4. **Usage**: Embedded scripts are included and dispatched via command registries like `FoldseekBase.cpp`.

Sources: [data/CMakeLists.txt:1-39](), [src/CMakeLists.txt:33](), [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:1-120]()

## SIMD, GPU, and Static Build Flags

### CPU Optimization (SIMD)
The build system detects and propagates SIMD flags. For example, if `HAVE_SSE2` is detected without `SSE4.1`, `ENABLE_PROSTT5` is automatically disabled because the underlying language model requires higher-level SIMD instructions [CMakeLists.txt:70-73]().

### GPU Support (CUDA)
When `ENABLE_CUDA` is set to `1` [CMakeLists.txt:12]():
- The `HAVE_CUDA` macro is defined globally on `foldseek-framework` [src/CMakeLists.txt:28-30]().
- For ProstT5, `GGML_CUDA`, `GGML_CUDA_F16`, and `GGML_CUDA_FORCE_CUBLAS` are enabled to offload tensor operations to the GPU [CMakeLists.txt:105-110]().

### StrucTTY and Optional Flags
The `ENABLE_STRUCTTY` flag (default `1`) controls whether the terminal structure viewer is compiled, linking `lib/structty` and checking for required stb headers [CMakeLists.txt:13](), [CMakeLists.txt:47-62]().

### Static Linking
To create portable binaries, `FORCE_STATIC_DEPS` can be enabled. This forces the use of `.a` suffixes for libraries and sets static linking flags like `-static -static-libgcc -static-libstdc++` [CMakeLists.txt:14-26]().

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:11-116](), [src/CMakeLists.txt:17-30]()

## Dependency and Submodule Management

FoldSeek manages several sub-libraries via `add_subdirectory`. Notably, it relies on a fork of the MMseqs2 framework included under `lib/mmseqs` [CMakeLists.txt:9-35]().

### Dependency Relationship Graph

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "External Libraries [lib/]"
        MMS["lib/mmseqs"]
        TDI["lib/3di"]
        PUL["lib/pulchra"]
        KER["lib/kerasify"]
        TMA["lib/tmalign"]
        FCOMP["lib/foldcomp"]
        PT5["lib/prostt5"]
        STY["lib/structty"]
    end

    MMS --- TDI
    MMS --- PUL
    MMS --- KER
    MMS --- TMA
    MMS --- FCOMP
    PT5 --- MMS
    STY --- MMS
```

- **Submodules**: Regression tests and specific components like `ggml-kompute` are managed as Git submodules [.gitmodules:1-11]().
- **Framework Mode**: The `FOLDSEEK_FRAMEWORK_ONLY` flag allows building libraries without the final `foldseek` executable, useful for embedding FoldSeek in other applications [CMakeLists.txt:37-40]().

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:33-62](), [.gitmodules:1-11](), [src/CMakeLists.txt:43-50]()

## Adding New Commands

To integrate a new command into the build system:
1. Add the source file to `src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt` or `src/workflow/CMakeLists.txt` [src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt:1-29](), [src/workflow/CMakeLists.txt:1-21]().
2. Define the command logic and parameter bindings.
3. Register the command in the `foldseekCommands` registry within `src/FoldseekBase.cpp`.
4. If the command uses a shell script workflow, add the `.sh` file to `data/CMakeLists.txt` under `COMPILED_RESOURCES` for resource compilation [data/CMakeLists.txt:3-31]().

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt:1-29](), [src/workflow/CMakeLists.txt:1-21](), [data/CMakeLists.txt:3-31](), [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:1-120]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page details the Continuous Integration (CI) and containerization configurations used to build, test, and distribute FoldSeek across platforms and hardware architectures. It covers the primary multi-stage `Dockerfile`, GPU-enabled container builds, the Azure Pipelines build matrix, macOS universal binary creation (`lipo`), GitHub Actions workflows, and artifact publishing mechanisms. For local compilation details, see [Build System](5.1).

---

## 1. Overview of CI and Docker Infrastructure

FoldSeek relies on a multi-pronged CI and distribution architecture combining GitHub Actions for container publishing and macOS checks with Azure Pipelines for deep matrix builds (including Linux static binaries, sanitizers, MPI, and GPU targets).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "CI Platforms"
        GH["GitHub Actions\n(.github/workflows/)"]
        AZ["Azure Pipelines\n(azure-pipelines.yml)"]
    end

    subgraph "Workflows and Jobs"
        GH_Docker["docker.yml\n(Multi-arch & GPU Images)"]
        GH_Mac["mac-arm64.yml\n(macOS ARM64 build)"]
        AZ_Ubuntu["build_ubuntu\n(AVX2, SSE4.1, MPI, ASan)"]
        AZ_GPU["build_ubuntu_gpu\n(Dockerfile.GPU-manylinux2014\nDockerfile.GPU-buster-cross-sbsa)"]
        AZ_Cross["build_ubuntu_cross\n(ARM64 cross-compile)"]
        AZ_Mac["build_macos\n(Universal lipo build via util/build_osx.sh)"]
    end

    GH --> GH_Docker
    GH --> GH_Mac
    AZ --> AZ_Ubuntu
    AZ --> AZ_GPU
    AZ --> AZ_Cross
    AZ --> AZ_Mac
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/docker.yml:1-141](), [.github/workflows/mac-arm64.yml:1-40](), [azure-pipelines.yml:1-180]()

---

## 2. Main Dockerfile & Multi-Architecture Build

The root `Dockerfile` employs a multi-stage build strategy using `debian:bookworm-slim` to compile instruction-set optimized binaries (`foldseek_sse41`, `foldseek_avx2`, `foldseek_arch`) and package them into a lightweight runtime image [Dockerfile:1-83]().

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Builder Stage [Dockerfile:2]"
        Base["debian:bookworm-slim"]
        Deps["Install crossbuild-essential\n& rustup toolchain [Dockerfile:7-27]"]
        
        subgraph "Compilation Targets"
            ArmBuild["arm64: cmake -DHAVE_ARM8=1\n-> /opt/build/foldseek_arch [Dockerfile:32-38]"]
            Avx2Build["x86_64: cmake -DHAVE_AVX2=1\n-> /opt/build/foldseek_avx2 [Dockerfile:43-51]"]
            SseBuild["x86_64: cmake -DHAVE_SSE4_1=1\n-> /opt/build/foldseek_sse41 [Dockerfile:53-63]"]
        end
    end

    subgraph "Runtime Stage [Dockerfile:66]"
        RuntimeBase["debian:bookworm-slim\n+ Runtime libs (gomp, zlib, aria2) [Dockerfile:74-76]"]
        Wrapper["util/foldseek_wrapper.sh\n(CPU flag detection entrypoint) [util/foldseek_wrapper.sh:1-10]"]
    end

    Base --> Deps
    Deps --> ArmBuild
    Deps --> Avx2Build
    Deps --> SseBuild
    
    ArmBuild --> RuntimeBase
    Avx2Build --> RuntimeBase
    SseBuild --> RuntimeBase
    RuntimeBase --> Wrapper
```

### Runtime Binary Selection

At container startup, `util/foldseek_wrapper.sh` inspects `/proc/cpuinfo` flags to select the optimal x86_64 instruction set variant:
- **AVX2**: Executes `/usr/local/bin/foldseek_avx2` if `avx2` is present in `/proc/cpuinfo` [util/foldseek_wrapper.sh:2-6]().
- **SSE4.1**: Falls back to `/usr/local/bin/foldseek_sse41` on legacy hardware [util/foldseek_wrapper.sh:7-9]().
- **ARM64**: Symlinks directly to `foldseek_arch` [Dockerfile:77-78]().

Sources: [Dockerfile:1-83](), [util/foldseek_wrapper.sh:1-10]()

---

## 3. GPU-Enabled Docker Builds & Compatibility Containers

For GPU-accelerated workloads (such as ProstT5 sequence embedding inference), FoldSeek builds specialized CUDA images using NVIDIA CUDA 12 SDK tooling (`cuda-nvcc-12-6`, `libcublas-dev-12-6`) targeting CUDA compute capabilities `75-real;80-real;86-real;89-real;90` [Dockerfile:13-17](), [Dockerfile:46]().

To guarantee robust compatibility across older Linux distributions, CI uses container-based compilation targets:
- **`Dockerfile.GPU-manylinux2014`**: Compiles x86_64 static binaries against `manylinux2014` base environments, enforcing strict symbol checks against GLIBC versions and filtering out unauthorized shared library dependencies [.github/workflows/Dockerfile.GPU-manylinux2014:1-35]().
- **`Dockerfile.GPU-buster-cross-sbsa`**: Cross-compiles ARM64/SBSA (Server Base System Architecture) GPU binaries using custom toolchain definitions [.github/workflows/Dockerfile.GPU-buster-cross-sbsa:1-32]().

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Dockerfile_GPU {
        +ARG GPU=1
        +CUDACXX /usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc
        +CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES "75-real;80-real;86-real;89-real;90"
    }
    class Manylinux2014 {
        +file: .github/workflows/Dockerfile.GPU-manylinux2014
        +checks GLIBC <= 2.17
        +static linking verification (ldd/readelf)
    }
    class SBSA_Cross {
        +file: .github/workflows/Dockerfile.GPU-buster-cross-sbsa
        +toolchain: /opt/toolchain.cmake
        +aarch64 static verification
    }

    Dockerfile_GPU --> Manylinux2014 : x86_64 pipeline
    Dockerfile_GPU --> SBSA_Cross : arm64 sbsa pipeline
```

Sources: [Dockerfile:13-51](), [.github/workflows/Dockerfile.GPU-manylinux2014:1-35](), [.github/workflows/Dockerfile.GPU-buster-cross-sbsa:1-32]()

---

## 4. Azure Pipelines Build Matrix & Cross-Compilation

Azure Pipelines (`azure-pipelines.yml`) manages deep matrix configurations covering static/dynamic linking, SIMD instruction sets, MPI support, address sanitizers, and cross-compilation [azure-pipelines.yml:10-156]().

| Job Name | Strategy Matrix / Environment | Key CMake Flags / Toolchain |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `build_ubuntu` | `avx2`, `sse41`, `avx2_mpi`, `asan` [azure-pipelines.yml:16-41] | `-DFORCE_STATIC_DEPS=1`, `-DHAVE_AVX2=1`, `-DHAVE_SANITIZER=1` [azure-pipelines.yml:60-65] |
| `build_ubuntu_gpu` | `x86_64` (manylinux2014), `aarch64` (sbsa) [azure-pipelines.yml:91-96] | Uses specialized Dockerfiles with CUDA enabled [azure-pipelines.yml:93-96] |
| `build_ubuntu_cross` | `arm64` (`CPREF: aarch64`) [azure-pipelines.yml:120-123] | `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc`, `-DHAVE_ARM8=1`, Rust target `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` [azure-pipelines.yml:145-149] |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "azure-pipelines.yml Execution"
        Matrix["Matrix Strategy\n(avx2, sse41, avx2_mpi, asan) [azure-pipelines.yml:15-41]"]
        GccSetup["Install GCC 11 & OpenMP static libs [azure-pipelines.yml:45-49]"]
        CMakeStep["Configure CMake & Compile foldseek [azure-pipelines.yml:56-68]"]
        RegTest["Run regression/run_regression.sh [azure-pipelines.yml:70-77]"]
        Publish["PublishPipelineArtifact@0\n-> foldseek-linux-[SIMD] [azure-pipelines.yml:78-83]"]
    end

    Matrix --> GccSetup
    GccSetup --> CMakeStep
    CMakeStep --> RegTest
    RegTest --> Publish
```

Sources: [azure-pipelines.yml:1-180]()

---

## 5. macOS Universal Binary Builds

macOS builds are handled both in Azure Pipelines (`build_macos`) and GitHub Actions (`mac-arm64.yml`), producing universal binaries supporting both Intel (`x86_64`) and Apple Silicon (`arm64`) architectures [.github/workflows/mac-arm64.yml:1-40](), [azure-pipelines.yml:157-180]().

The core orchestration for universal macOS packaging resides in `util/build_osx.sh`:
1. **OpenMP Runtime Compilation**: Downloads LLVM OpenMP source (`llvmorg-20.1.7`), building static `libomp.a` separately for `x86_64` and `arm64` [util/build_osx.sh:30-88]().
2. **Architecture-Specific CMake Passes**: Configures independent build dirs with `-DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES` set to `x86_64` and `arm64` respectively, linking static OpenMP [util/build_osx.sh:51-99]().
3. **Dependency and Deployment Target Validation**: Uses `otool -L` and `vtool` to ensure no unauthorized dynamic libraries are linked and that `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` adheres to bounds [util/build_osx.sh:62-73]().
4. **Universal Binary Stitching (`lipo`)**: Combines the compiled binaries into a universal executable [util/build_osx.sh:115-119]().

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "util/build_osx.sh"
        BuildOMP["Build LLVM OpenMP (libomp.a) for x86_64 & arm64 [util/build_osx.sh:30-88]"]
        BuildX64["CMake Configure & Build x86_64 binary [util/build_osx.sh:50-60]"]
        BuildARM["CMake Configure & Build arm64 binary [util/build_arm64:90-100]"]
        Verify["Validate otool -L & deployment target version [util/build_osx.sh:62-73]"]
        Lipo["lipo -create x86_64 and arm64 -> universal foldseek [util/build_osx.sh:115-119]"]
    end

    BuildOMP --> BuildX64
    BuildOMP --> BuildARM
    BuildX64 --> Verify
    BuildARM --> Verify
    Verify --> Lipo
```

Sources: [util/build_osx.sh:1-120](), [.github/workflows/mac-arm64.yml:1-40]()

---

## 6. GitHub Actions Workflows & Artifact Uploads

GitHub Actions automates continuous delivery through dedicated workflow YAML files:
- **`.github/workflows/docker.yml`**: Uses Docker Buildx and QEMU to build and push multi-platform images (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) and CUDA-enabled container variants to the GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io/steineggerlab/foldseek`) [.github/workflows/docker.yml:1-141]().
- **`.github/workflows/mac-arm64.yml`**: Compiles and runs regression verification tests on macOS runners [.github/workflows/mac-arm64.yml:1-40]().

Artifact uploads across CI providers utilize pipeline-native tasks (e.g., Azure `PublishPipelineArtifact@0`) to archive compiled executables like `foldseek-linux-AVX2` or `foldseek-mac-universal` for release tagging [azure-pipelines.yml:78-83]().

Sources: [.github/workflows/docker.yml:1-141](), [.github/workflows/mac-arm64.yml:1-40](), [azure-pipelines.yml:78-83]()

# Page: Testing Framework

# Testing Framework

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.github/results.png](.github/results.png)
- [README.md](README.md)
- [data/evalue_nn.kerasify](data/evalue_nn.kerasify)

- [src/commons/StructureSmithWaterman.h](src/commons/StructureSmithWaterman.h)
- [src/strucclustutils/EvalueNeuralNet.cpp](src/strucclustutils/EvalueNeuralNet.cpp)
- [src/strucclustutils/EvalueNeuralNet.h](src/strucclustutils/EvalueNeuralNet.h)
- [src/strucclustutils/LoLAlign.cpp](src/strucclustutils/LoLAlign.cpp)
- [src/strucclustutils/LoLAlign.h](src/strucclustutils/LoLAlign.h)
- [src/strucclustutils/LoLAlignProbability.h](src/strucclustutils/LoLAlignProbability.h)
- [src/strucclustutils/LoLAlignProbabilityWeights.h](src/strucclustutils/LoLAlignProbabilityWeights.h)
- [src/strucclustutils/samplemulambda.cpp](src/strucclustutils/samplemulambda.cpp)

</details>



This page describes how testing, regression verification, and parameter validation are implemented in the Foldseek codebase. The scope covers the regression test suite (`run_regression.sh`), example input files, the statistical parameter sampling utility (`samplemulambda`), and continuous integration pipelines ensuring correctness across CPU, SIMD, and GPU architectures.

## 1. Testing Architecture and Components

Foldseek relies on a combination of automated regression scripts, static test inputs, statistical sampling utilities, and continuous integration runners.

Title: Testing Framework Components to Code Entities
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph NaturalLanguage["Testing Components"]
        RT["Regression Test Suite"]
        SML["Parameter Sampling"]
        LC["Homology Classifier"]
    end
    
    subgraph CodeSpace["Code Entities"]
        Script["run_regression.sh"]
        Sample["src/strucclustutils/samplemulambda.cpp"]
        Prob["src/strucclustutils/LoLAlignProbability.h"]
        SSW["src/commons/StructureSmithWaterman.cpp"]
    end
    
    RT --> Script
    SML --> Sample
    LC --> Prob
    Sample --> SSW
```

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/samplemulambda.cpp:1-12](), [src/strucclustutils/LoLAlignProbability.h:1-12]()

## 2. Regression Testing Suite

The regression test suite validates end-to-end command execution and output stability against known gold-standard results. 

### 2.1 Regression Execution and Example Datasets
Regression testing is primarily orchestrated by shell scripts that invoke core binaries against benchmark files located in the `example/` directory. Standard protein structures such as `example/1tim.pdb.gz` and `example/8tim.pdb.gz` provide predictable folds for verifying alignment scores, Cα coordinate processing, and database indexing.

Sources: [README.md:97-99]()

## 3. Statistical Parameter Validation (`samplemulambda`)

To ensure accurate E-value estimation across arbitrary database sizes and sequence lengths, Foldseek uses the `samplemulambda` utility to fit Extreme Value Distribution (EVD) parameters ($\mu$ and $\lambda$) for alignment scores [src/strucclustutils/samplemulambda.cpp:77-96]().

### 3.1 Histogram Management and EVD Fitting
The utility relies on the internal `histogram_s` data structure to accumulate alignment scores and compute goodness-of-fit metrics [src/strucclustutils/samplemulambda.cpp:77-91](). The function `ExtremeValueP` evaluates the tail probability $P(S > x)$ for fitted parameters [src/strucclustutils/samplemulambda.cpp:119-132](), while `sre_random` implements L'Ecuyer's combined linear congruential generator for reproducible background score sampling [src/strucclustutils/samplemulambda.cpp:166-188]().

Title: Statistical Parameter Flow in samplemulambda
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant SML as samplemulambda.cpp
    participant SSW as StructureSmithWaterman
    participant EVD as ExtremeValueP

    SML->>SSW: alignScoreEndPos(db_aa, db_3di)
    SSW-->>SML: Return score s_align.score1
    SML->>SML: AddToHistogram(histogram_s, score)
    SML->>SML: ExtremeValueFitHistogram()
    SML->>EVD: ExtremeValueP(x, mu, lambda)
    EVD-->>SML: Return tail probability P(S>x)
```

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/samplemulambda.cpp:77-132](), [src/commons/StructureSmithWaterman.h:112-119]()

## 4. Homology Probability Classifier Validation

Foldseek validates its structural homology predictions via the `LoLAlignProbability` class, which extracts a 39-feature vector from alignment metrics, topological adjacency, and LDDT scores [src/strucclustutils/LoLAlignProbability.h:37-82]().

### 4.1 Weight Integration and Feature Extraction
The classifier uses pre-trained neural network weights stored in `LoLAlignProbabilityWeights.h` (`lolprobw::W0`, `lolprobw::FEAT_MEAN`, etc.) [src/strucclustutils/LoLAlignProbabilityWeights.h:10-35]() to compute homology probabilities during local alignments.

Title: Homology Classifier Architecture to Code Mapping
```mermaid
classDiagram
    class LoLAlign {
        -LoLAlignProbability lolProb
        -LDDTCalculator lddtcalc
        +align()
    }
    class LoLAlignProbability {
        +prepareQuery(queryLen, qx, qy, qz)
        +predict(targetLen, tx, ty, tz, qAln, tAln, nAln, evalue, bits, lddt, ...)
        -buildAdjacency()
        -buildResHist6()
    }
    class LoLAlignProbabilityWeights {
        <<namespace>> lolprobw
        +FEAT_MEAN[39]
        +FEAT_STD[39]
        +W0[1248]
    }
    LoLAlign --> LoLAlignProbability : uses
    LoLAlignProbability ..> LoLAlignProbabilityWeights : reads weights
```

Sources: [src/strucclustutils/LoLAlign.h:120-126](), [src/strucclustutils/LoLAlignProbability.h:19-82](), [src/strucclustutils/LoLAlignProbabilityWeights.h:10-35]()

## 5. Continuous Integration Environments

Automated testing is performed across multiple operating systems and hardware configurations using Azure Pipelines and containerized environments.

| Job Name | Target Architecture | Build Configuration | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `build_ubuntu` | x86_64 (AVX2 / SSE4.1) | Release | Standard binary verification |
| `build_ubuntu` | x86_64 (AVX2) | ASanOpt | Memory error and leak detection |
| `build_ubuntu_gpu` | x86_64 + CUDA | Release | GPU acceleration validation |
| `build_ubuntu_cross` | ARM64 (aarch64) | Release | Cross-compilation verification |
| `build_macos` | Universal (x86_64 / ARM64) | Release | macOS ecosystem verification |

Sources: [README.md:20](), [README.md:92-93]()

# Page: Adding New Commands

# Adding New Commands

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [data/CMakeLists.txt](data/CMakeLists.txt)
- [data/createinterfacedb.sh](data/createinterfacedb.sh)
- [src/FoldseekBase.cpp](src/FoldseekBase.cpp)
- [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h](src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h)
- [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp](src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp)
- [src/commons/LocalParameters.h](src/commons/LocalParameters.h)
- [src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt](src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt)
- [src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp](src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp)
- [src/strucclustutils/createstructinterfacedb.cpp](src/strucclustutils/createstructinterfacedb.cpp)
- [src/workflow/CMakeLists.txt](src/workflow/CMakeLists.txt)

</details>



This page provides a detailed guide for developers who want to extend FoldSeek by adding new commands to the system. It covers the command architecture, implementation steps, parameter management, workflow shell script creation, and integration into FoldSeek's build and CMake resource compilation systems. For information about the underlying command dispatch architecture, see [Command System](#2.1).

## Overview of the Command Architecture

FoldSeek's command system follows a modular architecture that separates command registration, implementation, and parameter handling. Understanding this architecture is essential before adding new commands.

### Natural Language to Code Entity Space: Architecture

The following diagram maps high-level system concepts to specific code entities in the FoldSeek repository.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Command Registration"
        FoldseekBase["FoldseekBase.cpp\nfoldseekCommands vector"]
        CommandStruct["Command Structure\n(Command.h)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Command Implementation"
        LocalCommandDecl["LocalCommandDeclarations.h\nextern int function()"]
        CommandImpl["Command Implementation\ne.g., StructureSearch.cpp"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Parameter System"
        LocalParams["LocalParameters.cpp/h\nLocalParameters class"]
        ParamVectors["std::vector<MMseqsParameter *>\nper-command lists"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Command Execution"
        Main["foldseek.cpp\nmain()"]
        Dispatch["Command dispatching logic"]
    end
    
    Main --> Dispatch
    FoldseekBase --> CommandStruct
    CommandStruct --> Dispatch
    LocalCommandDecl --> CommandImpl
    CommandImpl --> Dispatch
    LocalParams --> ParamVectors
    ParamVectors --> CommandStruct
```

Sources: [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:17-18](), [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:18-26](), [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h:1-36]()

## Step-by-Step Process for Adding a New Command

### 1. Implement the Command Function

Create a command implementation in an appropriate source file (usually within the `workflow` directory for high-level logic, or `strucclustutils/` for standalone utilities):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Command Implementation Function"
        Function["int cmdFunc(int argc, const char** argv, const Command &command)"]
        Parameters["LocalParameters::getLocalInstance()"]
        Logic["par.parseParameters(...)"]
        Result["return EXIT_SUCCESS"]
    end
    
    Function --> Parameters --> Logic --> Result
```

Key considerations:
- The function must have the signature `int functionName(int argc, const char** argv, const Command &command)` [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h:6-35]().
- Use `LocalParameters::getLocalInstance()` to access the singleton parameter object [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:21-26]().
- Call `par.parseParameters(argc, argv, command, ...)` to populate variables from the CLI [src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp:9-11]().

Sources: [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h:1-36](), [src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp:9-11]()

### 2. Declare the Command Function

Add your command declaration to `LocalCommandDeclarations.h`. This allows `FoldseekBase.cpp` to reference the function pointer via `extern` linkage.

Example:
```cpp
extern int mynewcommand(int argc, const char** argv, const Command &command);
```

Sources: [src/LocalCommandDeclarations.h:6-35]()

### 3. Define Command Parameters

If your command requires specific parameters, add them to `LocalParameters.cpp` and `LocalParameters.h`:

1. **Declare Parameter ID**: Add a unique ID in `Parameters.h` (inherited) or define it locally.
2. **Declare Parameter Vector**: In `LocalParameters.h`, add a `std::vector<MMseqsParameter *>` for your command [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:131-165]().
3. **Initialize in Constructor**: In `LocalParameters.cpp`, initialize any new `MMseqsParameter` objects with flags, regex validation, and pointers to storage variables [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:11-40]().
4. **Populate Vector**: In the `LocalParameters` constructor, `push_back` the relevant parameters into your new command's parameter vector.

Sources: [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:131-165](), [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:9-40]()

### 4. Register the Command

Add your command to the `foldseekCommands` vector in `FoldseekBase.cpp`. This registration includes the CLI name, the function pointer, the parameter vector, and metadata for the help menu and validation rules.

```cpp
{"my-command", mynewcommand, &localPar.mynewcommand_params, COMMAND_MAIN,
 "Description of what it does",
 "foldseek my-command input output",
 "Author Name <email>",
 "<i:inputDB> <o:outputDB>",
 CITATION_FOLDSEEK, 
 {{"inputDB", DbType::ACCESS_MODE_INPUT, DbType::NEED_DATA, &DbValidator::allDb },
  {"outputDB", DbType::ACCESS_MODE_OUTPUT, DbType::NEED_DATA, &DbValidator::allDb }}}
```

Sources: [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:17-41]()

### 5. Writing Workflow Shell Scripts and Resource Compilation

Many FoldSeek workflows orchestrate underlying binaries via shell scripts (e.g., `createinterfacedb`) [src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp:13-20](). To wire a workflow script into the codebase:
1. Write the shell script and place it in the `data/` directory (e.g., `data/createinterfacedb.sh`) [data/createinterfacedb.sh:1-45]().
2. Add the script filename to `COMPILED_RESOURCES` in `data/CMakeLists.txt` [data/CMakeLists.txt:3-31]().
3. During the build, the CMake system uses `MMseqsResourceCompiler` to compile resources into C++ headers (e.g., `createinterfacedb.sh.h`) [data/CMakeLists.txt:1, 33-37]().
4. Include the generated header in your utility or workflow implementation file, write the script to disk dynamically via `FileUtil::writeFile`, and execute it using `CommandCaller` [src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp:7, 13-20]().

Sources: [data/CMakeLists.txt:1-37](), [src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp:7-20](), [data/createinterfacedb.sh:1-45]()

### 6. Update the Build System

You must register your new source files in the appropriate CMake build lists:
- **Workflows**: Add source files to `workflow_source_files` in `src/workflow/CMakeLists.txt` [src/workflow/CMakeLists.txt:1-21]().
- **Utilities**: Add source files to `strucclustutils_source_files` in `src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt` [src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt:1-28]().

Sources: [src/workflow/CMakeLists.txt:1-21](), [src/strucclustutils/CMakeLists.txt:1-28]()

## Natural Language to Code Entity Space: Data Flow

This diagram illustrates how data flows from the Command Line Interface (CLI) through the parameter system into command execution and shell script orchestration.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "CLI Layer"
        CLI["User Input\n'foldseek createinterfacedb ...'"]
    end

    subgraph "Parameter Parsing"
        Registry["foldseekCommands\n(FoldseekBase.cpp)"]
        Parser["Parameters::parseParameters\n(LocalParameters.cpp)"]
    end

    subgraph "Logic Execution"
        ImplFunc["createinterfacedb()\n(createinterfacedb.cpp)"]
        ResHeader["createinterfacedb.sh.h\n(Generated Resource Header)"]
        CmdCaller["CommandCaller\n(Executes .sh script)"]
        ShellScript["createinterfacedb.sh\n(data/ resource)"]
    end

    CLI --> Registry
    Registry --> ImplFunc
    ImplFunc --> Parser
    ImplFunc --> ResHeader
    ResHeader --> ImplFunc
    ImplFunc --> CmdCaller
    CmdCaller --> ShellScript
```

Sources: [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:61-68](), [src/strucclustutils/createinterfacedb.cpp:9-20](), [data/createinterfacedb.sh:1-41](), [data/CMakeLists.txt:1-37]()

## Command Categories and Types

FoldSeek organizes commands into categories to control visibility in the help output and command-line usage.

| Category Constant | Description | File Reference |
|-------------------|-------------|----------------|
| `COMMAND_MAIN` | Primary user commands | [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:18]() |
| `COMMAND_EASY` | Simplified "easy-" wrappers | [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:92]() |
| `COMMAND_SET` | Database manipulation | [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:49]() |
| `COMMAND_HIDDEN` | Internal/Developer tools | [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:42]() |

Sources: [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:17-96]()

## Common Validator Types for Database Arguments

When registering a command, you must specify validators to ensure input/output paths are valid.

| Validator | Purpose | File Reference |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| `&DbValidator::flatfile` | Standard file on disk | [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:41]() |
| `&DbValidator::allDb` | Any MMseqs2/Foldseek DB | [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:60]() |
| `&DbValidator::directory` | Path must be a directory | [src/FoldseekBase.cpp:84]() |
| `&FoldSeekDbValidator::flatfileAndFolder` | Files or directories (Foldseek specific) | [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:10-16]() |

# Page: Vendored Libraries

# Vendored Libraries

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [lib/gemmi/mmcif.hpp](lib/gemmi/mmcif.hpp)
- [lib/gemmi/pdb.hpp](lib/gemmi/pdb.hpp)
- [lib/kerasify/LICENSE](lib/kerasify/LICENSE)
- [lib/mmseqs/.gitmodules](lib/mmseqs/.gitmodules)
- [lib/tmalign/LICENSE](lib/tmalign/LICENSE)
- [util/update_foldcomp.sh](util/update_foldcomp.sh)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
Foldseek bundles several third-party libraries and framework dependencies under the `lib/` directory. Vendoring these libraries ensures consistent builds across diverse operating systems, eliminates external package manager dependencies during compilation, and permits deep optimizations (such as custom SIMD vectorization and tightly integrated memory allocators) alongside the MMseqs2 ecosystem. This page surveys the primary vendored libraries, detailing their specific architectural roles, integration strategies, update mechanisms, and code pointers.

---

## 1. MMseqs2 Framework (`lib/mmseqs`)
The MMseqs2 framework forms the foundational backbone of Foldseek. It provides the multi-threaded execution engine, memory-mapped database input/output systems, vectorized sequence alignment routines, parameter parsing infrastructure, and core command dispatching framework.

Foldseek integrates MMseqs2 as a submodule or base framework, extending its command registry (`FoldseekBase.cpp`) and parameter classes (`LocalParameters`) to handle 3D structural data alongside standard sequence databases. Submodules like regression tests are managed under `lib/mmseqs/.gitmodules` [lib/mmseqs/.gitmodules:1-3]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "NaturalLanguageSpace"
        A["MMseqs2BaseEngine"]
        B["VectorizedDatabaseIO"]
    end
    subgraph "CodeEntitySpace"
        C["lib/mmseqs"]
        D["FoldseekBase.cpp"]
    end
    A --> C
    B --> C
    C --> D
```
*Diagram 1: MMseqs2 Integration Mapping*

Sources: `lib/mmseqs/.gitmodules:1-4`

---

## 2. Gemmi (`lib/gemmi`)
Gemmi is a high-performance C++ library used for parsing macromolecular structural data formats, specifically mmCIF (`PDBx/mmCIF`) and legacy PDB files. 

### Implementation & Data Flow
Gemmi parses coordinate files into rich memory representations (`Structure`, `Model`, `Chain`, `Residue`, `Atom`). Within `lib/gemmi/mmcif.hpp`, tabular data such as secondary structure elements are extracted using helper functions like `gemmi::impl::read_helices` and `gemmi::impl::read_sheets` [lib/gemmi/mmcif.hpp:96-121](). Coordinate transformations, anisotropic temperature factors, and sequence identifiers are resolved through robust string-to-numeric converters.

Similarly, `lib/gemmi/pdb.hpp` implements fixed-column parsing rules conforming to wwPDB specifications, incorporating extensions for hybrid-36 serial numbers (`gemmi::pdb_impl::read_serial`) [lib/gemmi/pdb.hpp:137-140](), two-character chain IDs, and crystallographic symmetry matrices (`gemmi::pdb_impl::read_matrix`) [lib/gemmi/pdb.hpp:100-111]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "ParsingPipeline"
        A["RawmmCIFPDBFile"] --> B["gemmi::impl::read_helices\nlib/gemmi/mmcif.hpp:96-120"]
        A --> C["gemmi::pdb_impl::read_matrix\nlib/gemmi/pdb.hpp:100-111"]
        B --> D["gemmi::Structure"]
        C --> D
    end
```
*Diagram 2: Gemmi Structure Parsing Data Flow*

Sources: `lib/gemmi/mmcif.hpp:96-121`, `lib/gemmi/pdb.hpp:100-140`

---

## 3. Foldcomp (`lib/foldcomp`)
Foldcomp provides ultra-fast compression and decompression for massive protein structure databases (such as AlphaFold DB predictions). 

### Integration and Updates
Foldcomp is integrated into Foldseek to enable direct reading and querying of compressed structure repositories without requiring explicit pre-decompression to individual PDB/mmCIF files. The library is updated via subtree synchronization scripts located in the repository, specifically `util/update_foldcomp.sh`, which pulls from the upstream repository using git subtree merge strategies [util/update_foldcomp.sh:1-2]().

Sources: `util/update_foldcomp.sh:1-3`

---

## 4. TM-align (`lib/tmalign`)
TM-align is the standard algorithm for protein structure alignment and TM-score calculation. 

### Integration
Bundled under `lib/tmalign`, the library operates independently of sequence identity to compute optimal rotations, translations, and residue-residue equivalence between two protein structures. Its licensing and attribution terms are preserved in `lib/tmalign/LICENSE` [lib/tmalign/LICENSE:1-12](). Foldseek invokes TM-align routines during detailed rescoring steps of structure searches and alignments.

Sources: `lib/tmalign/LICENSE:1-13`

---

## 5. Pulchra (`lib/pulchra`)
Pulchra is a C++ library integrated to rebuild full atomic coordinate models (backbone and side-chain approximations) starting from reduced $C_\alpha$ trace representations. In Foldseek workflows, when models are processed or compressed where only $C_\alpha$ traces are retained, Pulchra provides the geometric reconstruction necessary for full atom-based visualization or interface analysis.

Sources: `lib/pulchra/` (directory integration)

---

## 6. Kerasify (`lib/kerasify`)
Kerasify is a lightweight C++ library designed to load and evaluate pre-trained Keras neural network models directly in C++ without requiring heavy Python or TensorFlow runtimes.

### Integration
Kerasify evaluates the small neural network weights utilized by downstream modules (such as the 3Di structural alphabet prediction networks). Model definitions and weights are serialized and executed efficiently via `lib/kerasify/`, maintaining zero external machine learning library dependencies at runtime. Licensing information is tracked in `lib/kerasify/LICENSE` [lib/kerasify/LICENSE:1-59]().

Sources: `lib/kerasify/LICENSE:1-59`

---

## 7. 3Di (`lib/3di`)
The `lib/3di` component encompasses the encoder architecture and scoring matrices (such as `mat3di`) that translate 3D backbone local geometries into the 1D discrete structural alphabet (3Di states). It works alongside `structureto3didescriptor` utilities to convert coordinate databases into searchable discrete sequence representations that can be processed with standard sequence-alignment speeds.

Sources: `lib/3di/` (directory integration)

---

## 8. ProstT5 / ggml (`lib/prostt5`)
ProstT5 is a bilingual protein language model mapping between protein sequences and 3Di structural sequences. 

### Integration
Foldseek incorporates a ggml-based implementation under `lib/prostt5` to execute ProstT5 inference locally on both CPU and GPU architectures. By leveraging ggml tensors and quantization routines, the model runs efficiently within C++ memory limits, predicting 3Di states directly from amino acid inputs without relying on external Python execution environments.

Sources: `lib/prostt5/` (directory integration)

---

## 9. StrucTTY (`lib/structty`)
StrucTTY provides terminal-based ASCII visualization of 3D protein structures.

### Integration
Integrated via `lib/structty`, this library powers the `structty` command-line utility. It parses residue coordinates and renders interactive or static color-coded ASCII/ANSI graphical representations of protein chains and interfaces directly in standard terminal emulators.

Sources: `lib/structty/` (directory integration)

---

## Purpose and Scope
This page defines codebase-specific terms, jargon, abbreviations, and domain concepts used across the Foldseek repository. It serves as a reference for onboarding engineers to understand structural biology metrics, internal data abstractions, and core algorithmic components with direct pointers to the source code.

## 1. Structural Representation & Metrics

### 3Di (3D-Interactions)
A structural alphabet that discretizes the tertiary interactions of a residue with its nearest neighbors in 3D space. 3Di sequences allow Foldseek to treat structure alignment as a sequence alignment problem, leveraging optimized SIMD-accelerated Smith-Waterman implementations from MMseqs2.
*   **Implementation:** Handled via the 3Di modules and translation scripts [lib/3di/structureto3di.h:1-12](), [lib/3di/structureto3di.cpp:1-50]().
*   **Data Type:** Stored internally and processed with specialized substitution matrices like `mat3di.out` [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:4-4](), [data/mat3di.out:1-20]().

### TM-score (Template Modeling Score)
A metric assessing topological similarity between two protein structures, ranging from (0, 1], where >0.5 implies the same fold.
*   **Implementation:** Calculated via the `TMaligner` class [src/commons/TMaligner.h:1-20](), [src/commons/TMaligner.cpp:1-100]().
*   **Thresholds:** Controlled by `--tmscore-threshold` and `--tmscore-threshold-mode` [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:11-12](), [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:50-54]().

### LDDT (Local Distance Difference Test)
A superposition-independent metric comparing local residue environments, essential for predicted structure validation.
*   **Implementation:** `LDDTCalculator` uses grid-based neighbor searches within a cutoff [src/commons/LDDT.h:13-20](), [src/commons/LDDT.cpp:1-50]().
*   **Internal Data:** `LDDTScoreResult` stores per-residue and average scores [src/commons/LDDT.h:97-150]().

### Structure Bits
A heuristic scoring metric used for ranking hits, calculated as `bits * sqrt(alnlddt * alntmscore)`.
*   **Parameter:** Enabled via `--sort-by-structure-bits` [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:15-15]().

Sources: [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:4-15](), [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:50-54](), [src/commons/TMaligner.h:1-20](), [src/commons/LDDT.h:13-150](), [lib/3di/structureto3di.h:1-12]()

---

## 2. Internal Data Structures

### Coordinate16
A memory-efficient representation of protein coordinates supporting float or compressed `uint16_t` difference modes.
*   **Implementation:** [src/commons/Coordinate16.h:1-30](), [src/commons/LocalParameters.cpp:25-25]().

### ChainToChainAln
Stores the alignment between two specific chains from different complexes, including the rotation matrix (`u`) and translation vector (`t`).
*   **Implementation:** [src/strucclustutils/MultimerUtil.h:41-117]().
*   **Superposition Vector:** 12-element array holding 3x3 rotation and 3x1 translation [src/strucclustutils/MultimerUtil.h:18-18](), [src/strucclustutils/MultimerUtil.h:75-86]().

### Assignment & SearchResult
Used in `scoremultimer` to aggregate chain-to-chain alignments, evaluate complex TM-scores, and manage complex-level states.
*   **Implementation:** [src/strucclustutils/scoremultimer.cpp:22-160]().

### ComplexDataHandler
Holds complex-level scores such as query/target complex TM-scores, coverage metrics, chain TM-scores, and interface LDDT scores.
*   **Implementation:** [src/strucclustutils/MultimerUtil.h:153-168]().

### KeyIterator
An abstract interface (`DbKeyIterator`, `MapIterator`) used by `convert2pdb` to iterate over database keys or complex groupings.
*   **Implementation:** [src/strucclustutils/convert2pdb.cpp:18-63]().

Sources: [src/commons/Coordinate16.h:1-30](), [src/strucclustutils/MultimerUtil.h:18-168](), [src/strucclustutils/scoremultimer.cpp:22-160](), [src/strucclustutils/convert2pdb.cpp:18-63]()

---

## 3. Algorithm Concepts

### 3Di+AA Alignment
A hybrid alignment mode combining structural 3Di alphabets with amino acid sequence evolutionary profiles (`alignmentType = 2`).
*   **Implementation:** [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:38-38](), [src/strucclustutils/structurealign.cpp:32-35]().

### LoLAlign (Local-over-Local Alignment)
A specialized probabilistic alignment algorithm designed to detect local structural domains within larger, divergent proteins (`ALIGNMENT_TYPE_LOLALIGN = 3`).
*   **Implementation & Weights:** `LoLAlign` class, `LoLAlignProbability`, and `LoLAlignProbabilityWeights` [src/strucclustutils/LoLAlign.h:20-126](), [src/strucclustutils/LoLAlign.cpp:1-214]().

### Neural Network E-value Estimation
Uses pre-trained neural networks via `kerasify` to estimate statistical E-values for structural alignments since structural scores deviate from standard sequence score distributions.
*   **Implementation:** [lib/kerasify/keras_model.h:1-20](), [data/encoder_weights_3di.kerasify:1-10]().

Sources: [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:38-38](), [src/strucclustutils/structurealign.cpp:32-35](), [src/strucclustutils/LoLAlign.h:20-126](), [src/strucclustutils/LoLAlign.cpp:1-214]()

---

| `ALIGNMENT_TYPE_TMALIGN` | 1 | Global structural alignment using TM-align [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:37-37]() |
| `ALIGNMENT_TYPE_3DI_AA` | 2 | Hybrid 3Di + amino acid alignment [src/commons/LocalParameters.h:38-38]() |
